# 00 — Overview: ETAutomations without a browser

## 1. The question and the short answer

**Question:** can the ETAutomations pipeline (carrier ETA lookup → QuickBooks invoice update + e-mail →
VShipCRM note + ETA) run without Playwright or any other browser-driving workflow, so that it is faster?

**Answer: yes.** Every browser step in the original has a direct-API replacement. Two of them (QuickBooks
e-mail subject and the QuickBooks ETA date field) have one unverifiable detail each, which the program checks
on first use before it touches a customer. One carrier (MSC) needs a short manual step per run until MSC
approves official API access.

| Step | Original (browser?) | New (no browser) | Status / prerequisite |
|---|---|---|---|
| QuickBooks login | Persistent Chromium profile + password autofill | OAuth refresh token (already used by the original for lookups) | Ready (04 §5) |
| Find invoice, paid / partially paid | One REST query per row + reading the page | One batched query per 25 rows; `Balance`/`TotalAmt` | Ready (04 §6.3) |
| Set ETA custom field, change invoice number | Typing into the QBO web app (`slow_mo=200`, fixed sleeps) | One sparse update per invoice, verified after writing | Date-field write shape **UNVERIFIED** → probe `--write-test`; fallbacks in 04 §8 |
| E-mail the invoice with an ETA subject | "Review and send" dialog, type subject, Send | QBO `/send` with a temporarily swapped template subject (serialized, crash-safe); or company mailbox via Microsoft Graph/SMTP with the QBO PDF + pay link | Must pass the one-time `--send-test` before any customer e-mail (04b §10) |
| MSC ETA | Headless login every 30 min + **new browser per booking** | Official MSC DCSA Track & Trace API (subscription key) — or, until approved, the same GraphQL query over plain HTTP with a token pasted from the user's own signed-in browser | API needs MSC onboarding; `EBKG` support **UNVERIFIED** (06 §2) |
| Maersk ETA | **Headful Chrome per booking** behind Akamai | Official Maersk "Track & Trace Events" API (DCSA 2.2, OAuth client credentials) | Needs product approval on the existing developer app (07 §2) |
| CMA CGM ETA | **Headful Chrome per booking** behind DataDome, sometimes a human CAPTCHA | Official CMA "Logistic Tracking service API" (DCSA 2.2, API key) | Self-service 30-day trial, then a contract; billed per call (08 §2) |
| Grimaldi ETA | Not implemented | Not implemented (parity) — Grimaldi has no public API and is not a DCSA member; possibly via the aggregator | see 09 Part C |
| Any carrier while approval is pending | — | Optional licensed aggregator, **ShipsGo API v2** (1 credit per new booking; asynchronous — a newly registered booking may need a later run before data appears) | see 09 Part B |
| VShipCRM | Already plain HTTP | Same endpoints, async, cached, one lookup per booking | Ready (05) |

Explicitly **not** done (by design): no browser automation of any kind; no workarounds for bot protection
(Akamai, DataDome, CAPTCHAs, TLS-fingerprint impersonation, telemetry replay); no automated myMSC sign-in;
no calls to QuickBooks' private web-app endpoints. Where an official API is not yet available, the program
says so clearly and the row goes to `Failed_To_Process.txt` for manual handling — the same outcome as a
failed lookup today — or to an optional licensed aggregator (09).

## 2. Why it is faster

Per actionable row the original spends roughly:

| Work | Original | New |
|---|---|---|
| Carrier lookup | MSC 4–8 s · Maersk 15–40 s · CMA 10–60 s (browser launch, warm-ups, pop-up timeouts) | ~0.3–1.5 s per HTTP call, 2–4 carrier calls in flight per carrier |
| QuickBooks update + e-mail | ~20–40 s of SPA page loads, `slow_mo=200` ms per action, 400–1 500 ms sleeps | ~1–3 s (1 update + e-mail calls) |
| VShip | 2–4 searches per row | 1 search + 1 comments read per booking, cached |
| Ordering | strictly one row after another | all reads concurrent (plan), writes concurrent across rows (apply) |

For a ~500-row file (the sample in the original's history had 494 rows: ~63% MSC, ~29% Maersk) that is
**several hours today** versus an estimated **10–20 minutes**, most of it the e-mail sends (which are
serialized under the template-swap strategy). These are estimates; the run report records actual timings.

## 3. Architecture

```
            eta run file.csv [--dry-run] [--yes] [--no-email]
                               │
                 ┌─────────────▼──────────────┐
                 │ pipeline.py                │
                 │  Phase 0 preflight (lock,  │
                 │   config, auth)            │
                 │  Phase 1 read + classify   │──── rules.py / texts.py / business_days.py (pure)
                 │  Phase 2 PLAN (reads only, │
                 │   concurrent)              │
                 │  Phase 3 review + confirm  │──── reports/run_<id>.csv|json
                 │  Phase 4 APPLY (writes)    │──── Send2*.txt, Failed_To_Process.txt, ledger.jsonl
                 │  Phase 5 summary           │
                 └──┬──────────┬───────────┬──┘
                    │          │           │
           ┌────────▼───┐ ┌────▼─────┐ ┌───▼───────────────────────────────┐
           │ qbo/       │ │ vship/   │ │ carriers/router.py (memo, breaker)│
           │ auth,      │ │ client,  │ │  msc.py  maersk.py  cma.py        │
           │ client,    │ │ logic    │ │  dcsa.py (shared parser)          │
           │ email      │ │          │ │  grimaldi.py  aggregator.py       │
           └─────┬──────┘ └────┬─────┘ └───┬───────────────────────────────┘
                 │             │           │
          http.py (httpx, retries, rate limits, redaction) · auth.py · token_store.py
```

Key properties:
- **Reads first, writes later.** Nothing changes anywhere until the plan has been shown and confirmed
  (`--dry-run` stops after the plan; `--yes` skips the prompt for scheduled use).
- **Exactly-once e-mail.** No send is ever retried after it may have reached the server; a same-day ledger
  blocks accidental re-sends; the QBO template swap is crash-recoverable.
- **Parity.** Every decision and text string of the original is specified in 01 with golden values taken by
  running the original code; every change is a labelled, reviewable deviation (D1…, CMA-D1…).
- **Configurable per carrier.** `ETA_PROVIDER_<CARRIER>` = native | aggregator | off, so a carrier whose API
  access is pending never blocks the others.

## 4. Biggest risks and how the design handles them

| Risk | Handling |
|---|---|
| QBO API cannot write the ETA **date** custom field in production (reported by others) | Every write is verified by reading back; `eta probe qbo --write-test` before go-live; fallbacks: string custom field or Ship date (04 §8.1) |
| QBO `/send` has no subject parameter | Template-swap with recovery file, lock, restore-in-finally and a mandatory human-confirmed send test; Graph/SMTP mailbox fallback (04b) |
| MSC official API may not accept `EBKG…` references / onboarding takes weeks | Token bridge keeps today's exact GraphQL query working; `eta probe msc --compare` validates the API before switching (06 §10) |
| Maersk product approval pending | Maersk rows fail cleanly ("not configured") or use the aggregator (09) |
| CMA trial ends / per-call billing | One call per booking per run (memo), 404s never retried, probe warns before billable calls (08) |
| Behaviour drift from the original | Golden tests (12), deviations list (01 §15), parity spot-check (13 §4, §7) |
| Concurrent runs | OS-level single-instance lock (03 §14) |

# 01 — Business rules (exact port of the original behaviour)

This file specifies **what** the program decides for every input row. It is a
line-by-line port of `mainIG.py`, `carrierTing/carriers.py`,
`stringTing/subjectEdit.py`, `QBTings/invoiceProcessing.py` (the decision parts),
`VShip/customerLookUp.py`, `VShip/noteSearch.py`, `VShip/writeNotif.py` and
`VShip/bookingLookUp.py` from the original `ETAutomations` repository.

**How** each external call is made lives in 04–09; **how** the run is
orchestrated (plan → confirm → apply, concurrency) lives in 10.

Everything here is implemented as **pure functions** in `rules.py`,
`texts.py`, `business_days.py` and `vship/logic.py` (no I/O), so it can be unit
tested exhaustively (see 12-testing.md).

Changes from the original are labelled **D1…Dn** (deliberate deviations, §15).
Quirks kept on purpose are labelled **O1…On** (§16). Nothing else may differ.

---

## 1. Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **DocNumber** | The QuickBooks invoice number. In this business it is the carrier booking number, sometimes followed by staff annotations (`EBKG12345678 A`, `NAM1234567 C`, `267546627/$150/RlsR`). The first CSV column holds it **exactly as it appears in QuickBooks**. |
| **Base booking** | The carrier booking number with the notification suffix removed (`EBKG12345678 A` → `EBKG12345678`). |
| **Notif #1 / #2** | First / second post-arrival notice e-mailed to the customer. Recorded twice: (a) a VShip internal comment containing `NOTIF #1`/`NOTIF #2`, (b) an `A` appended to the QBO DocNumber (`X` → `X A` → `X AA`). |
| **Window** | ETA ≤ now + 6 US business days (§5). Arrived shipments (ETA in the past) are always "in window". |
| **run_now** | `clock.now()` captured once at the start of the run (03-foundations §3). `today = run_now.date()`. |

## 2. Input file

- Path chosen by the user (CLI argument or Tk file dialog — 11-cli.md). Must exist, be a file, and have
  a `.csv` extension (case-insensitive) — same validation as `tinkyWinky.is_valid_txt_file`.
- Read with `open(path, "r", newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig")` and `csv.reader` (default dialect).
- Skip rows that are empty lists (blank lines).
- For each remaining row (1-based `line_no` = physical row index among non-blank rows, starting at 1):
  - `doc_number = row[0].strip()`
  - `amount_raw = row[1].strip() if len(row) > 1 else ""`
  - `amount = Decimal(amount_raw.replace(",", "").replace("$", "").strip())` → on `InvalidOperation`
    (or empty string) the row is **MALFORMED** (§7.1). (The original used `float`; `Decimal` gives the
    same comparisons for money values and avoids binary rounding.)
  - `doc_number == ""` → **MALFORMED** too (**D1**: the original crashed with `IndexError`).
- **D2 (header row):** if the **first** row is MALFORMED, its amount cell is non-numeric, and its first
  cell contains no digit (e.g. `Num,Amount`), skip it silently with an INFO log instead of reporting it.
- Duplicate DocNumbers in one file: process only the first occurrence; later ones are reported as
  `[SKIP] #<doc> - duplicate row in input file (line N)` in Failed_To_Process.txt (**D3**: the original
  would process — and possibly e-mail — the same invoice twice in one run).

## 3. Row classification (suffix rules)

Evaluate in this exact order (`last = doc_number[-1].lower()`):

| # | Condition | Kind | Base booking |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | row is MALFORMED | `MALFORMED` | — |
| 1 | `last` is a digit `0-9` | `STANDARD` | `doc_number` |
| 2 | `last == "a"` and `doc_number[-2:].lower() == "aa"` | `BOTH_SENT` | `doc_number[:-2].strip()` |
| 3 | `last == "a"` and `re.search(r"(?i)[^a]a$", doc_number)` | `NOTIF1_SENT` | `doc_number[:-1].strip()` |
| 4 | `last == "a"` (only possible for the 1-char DocNumber `"a"`) | `MANUAL` | — (**D4**: original silently did nothing) |
| 5 | `last == "r"` | `SKIP_R` | — |
| 6 | anything else | `MANUAL` | — |

The base booking is then `.strip().upper()`-ed for carrier routing and VShip searches (**D5**, harmless:
the original was case-sensitive). The **QBO lookup always uses `doc_number` exactly as in the file**.

Then the amount threshold (`ETA_MIN_INVOICE_AMOUNT`, default `1000`) applies to kinds
`STANDARD`, `NOTIF1_SENT`, `BOTH_SENT` **before anything else** (including before the BOTH_SENT → Ben
routing): `amount < 1000` → route **BINDU** (§7.2). It does **not** apply to `SKIP_R`/`MANUAL`
(the amount must still parse, though — MALFORMED is checked first for every row, exactly as the original).

Examples (all with amount `2,450.00` unless stated):

| doc_number | Kind | Base booking | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| `EBKG17208602` | STANDARD | `EBKG17208602` | carrier lookup |
| `267546627` | STANDARD | `267546627` | carrier lookup |
| `EBKG17208602 A` | NOTIF1_SENT | `EBKG17208602` | carrier lookup |
| `EBKG17208602a` | NOTIF1_SENT | `EBKG17208602` | carrier lookup |
| `EBKG17208602 AA` | BOTH_SENT | `EBKG17208602` | BEN |
| `EBKG17208602AA` | BOTH_SENT | `EBKG17208602` | BEN |
| `EBKG17208602 AA`, amount `850.00` | BOTH_SENT | `EBKG17208602` | BINDU (amount check first) |
| `EBKG17208602 A R` | SKIP_R | — | SKIPPED |
| `NAM1234567 C` | MANUAL | — | FAILED (raw doc_number line) |
| `267546627/$150/RlsR` | SKIP_R | — | SKIPPED |
| `EBKG17208602`, amount `abc` | MALFORMED | — | FAILED (malformed message) |

## 4. Carrier routing (`carriers/router.py`)

Applied to the base booking `b` (already stripped + upper-cased), in this order:

| Order | Test | Carrier | Query token |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `m = re.search(r"EBKG\d{8}", b)` | MSC | `m.group(0)` |
| 2 | `re.fullmatch(r"2\d{8}", b)` | Maersk | `b` |
| 3 | `m = re.search(r"NAM\d{7}", b)` | CMA | `m.group(0)` |
| 4 | `m = re.search(r"S3\d{8}", b)` | Grimaldi | `m.group(0)` |
| 5 | `re.search(r"20\d{8}", b)` | — reference number | → `UnsupportedCarrierError(f"This is a Ref Number: {b}")` |
| 6 | otherwise | — | → `UnsupportedCarrierError(f"No carrier pattern matched booking {b} — process manually")` |

- **D6 (extra text):** if `b != query token` for MSC/CMA/Grimaldi (e.g. `EBKG17208602 C 2`), raise
  `CarrierLookupError(f"Booking '{b}' contains text besides the {carrier} booking number {token} — process manually")`.
  The original sent the whole string to the carrier and failed later with a less clear error; the outcome
  (row lands in Failed_To_Process.txt as a carrier-lookup failure) is the same.
- **D7 (reference numbers):** the original matched only `2026\d{6}`; the new pattern `20\d{8}` (10 digits
  starting `20`) keeps working after 2026. It cannot collide with Maersk (exactly 9 digits, `fullmatch`).
- Grimaldi: `UnsupportedCarrierError(f"Grimaldi ETA lookup not yet implemented for booking {b}")` unless an
  aggregator provider is configured for it (09-dcsa-aggregators-grimaldi.md).
- Provider selection per carrier (`ETA_PROVIDER_<CARRIER>` = native | aggregator | off) is resolved by the
  router — see 09.

## 5. Time rules (`business_days.py`, `rules.py`)

```python
def add_business_days(start: datetime, n: int) -> datetime:
    # EXACT parity with the original: pandas CustomBusinessDay(calendar=USFederalHolidayCalendar())
    # start + n * CustomBusinessDay  (time of day is preserved; a weekend/holiday start rolls forward
    # as the first step)
def window_cutoff(run_now: datetime, business_days: int = 6) -> datetime: return add_business_days(run_now, business_days)
def in_window(eta: datetime, cutoff: datetime) -> bool: return eta <= cutoff
```

Comparisons (all naive datetimes; ETA is carrier-local wall time, run_now is machine-local — O1):

| Purpose | Rule | Used in |
|---|---|---|
| In 6-business-day window | `eta <= window_cutoff(run_now)` | §6 |
| Subject "arrived" branch | `eta <= run_now` | §8 |
| Subject "estimated" branch | `eta >= run_now` | §8 |
| Append `A` to DocNumber | `eta.date() <= today` | §9 |
| VShip note "ARRIVED" vs "ARRIVING" | `eta < run_now` | §10 |
| Notif #1 "done in the last week" | `notif1_created > run_now - timedelta(days=7)` | §11 |

Golden vectors for `window_cutoff` (generated with the original pandas implementation; tests must reproduce them):

| run_now | weekday | cutoff | weekday |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-05 09:30 | Thu | 2026-11-16 09:30 | Mon |
| 2026-11-06 16:00 | Fri | 2026-11-17 16:00 | Tue |
| 2026-11-07 10:00 | Sat | 2026-11-17 10:00 | Tue |
| 2026-11-08 23:59 | Sun | 2026-11-17 23:59 | Tue |
| 2026-11-09 08:00 | Mon | 2026-11-18 08:00 | Wed |
| 2026-11-11 12:00 | Wed | 2026-11-19 12:00 | Thu |
| 2026-11-23 07:15 | Mon | 2026-12-02 07:15 | Wed |
| 2026-11-26 09:00 | Thu | 2026-12-04 09:00 | Fri |
| 2026-12-18 17:45 | Fri | 2026-12-29 17:45 | Tue |
| 2026-12-24 08:00 | Thu | 2027-01-05 08:00 | Tue |
| 2026-12-31 13:00 | Thu | 2027-01-11 13:00 | Mon |
| 2027-01-15 10:00 | Fri | 2027-01-26 10:00 | Tue |
| 2027-02-12 10:00 | Fri | 2027-02-23 10:00 | Tue |

(pandas' calendar includes observed dates, e.g. 2027-12-31 for New Year 2028 and 2026-07-03 for July 4th 2026.)

Worked example: run_now = Thu 2026-11-05 09:30 → cutoff Mon 2026-11-16 09:30. An MSC ETA of
2026-11-16 (00:00) is in window; an ETA that carries a time of day, e.g. 2026-11-16 14:00 (CMA, or Maersk
with `MAERSK_ETA_DATE_ONLY=false` — 07 §7.5), is not. Maersk ETAs default to 00:00 for parity with the
date-only maersk.com page the original scraped.

## 6. Decision flow per row

Notation: `doc` = doc_number, `base` = base booking, `F(...)` = append an entry to
Failed_To_Process.txt (exact templates in §14), counters per §13.

```
MALFORMED            → F(malformed message)                                         [failed]
SKIP_R               → log "Don't need to do this one, ends in R"                   [skipped]
MANUAL               → F(doc)   (just the raw doc_number)                           [failed]
STANDARD / NOTIF1_SENT / BOTH_SENT with amount < threshold
                     → BINDU row [doc, amount_raw, customer_name(base)]            [routed]
BOTH_SENT            → BEN line doc                                                 [routed]

STANDARD / NOTIF1_SENT (amount ≥ threshold):
  1. eta = carrier.get_eta(token)                       (§4 router; errors → §6.1)
  2. cutoff = window_cutoff(run_now); in_window = eta.eta <= cutoff
  3. if in_window:
       a. notif = vship notif status for base           (§11; error → §6.2)
       b. notif.count == 2                → BEN line doc                            [routed]
       c. not notif.have_to_do            → F("[SKIP] #{doc} - Done in the last week")  [failed]  (D8)
       d. inv = QBO invoice with DocNumber == doc (exact) ; missing → F("[SKIP] #{doc} - not found in QuickBooks") [failed]
       e. if inv.is_paid:                 → PAID_UPDATE                             (§6.3)
          elif inv.is_partially_paid and tr_swb_found(base comments):
                                          → ACCOUNTING line                         [routed]
          else:                           → NOTIFY                                  (§6.4)
     else (outside window):
       d'. inv lookup as in d; missing → F("[SKIP] #{doc} - not found in QuickBooks") [failed]  (D9)
       e'.                                → FUTURE_UPDATE                           (§6.5)
```

### 6.1 Carrier lookup errors (both kinds)

| Exception from `get_eta` | Entry | Counter |
|---|---|---|
| `CarrierLookupError` (incl. `UnsupportedCarrierError`) | `[ERROR] #{doc} - Carrier Lookup Failed.\n{err}\n` | failed |
| `NoEtaError` | `[ERROR] #{doc} -  Can't determine ETA.\n{err}\n` (two spaces after `-`, O2) | failed |
| `CustomsHoldError` | PotentialCustomsHold.txt: `[ERROR] #{doc} -  Possible Customs Hold.` | failed |
| any other exception | `[ERROR] #{doc} - Unexpected error during carrier lookup.\n{err}\n` | failed |

The original's separate "ETA not found" path (carrier returned `None`) no longer exists:
`get_eta` raises `NoEtaError` instead (03-foundations §9), so those rows get the "Can't determine ETA." entry (**D10**).

### 6.2 VShip notif-lookup errors

Setting `ETA_ON_NOTIF_LOOKUP_ERROR` = `send` (default, **parity**) | `fail`.
- `send`: log WARNING `Notif lookup failed: {err} — defaulting to False` and continue with
  `NotifStatus(count=0, have_to_do=True)` — exactly what the original did (the QBO e-mail is the priority;
  the VShip note step will then fail visibly and be reported).
- `fail`: `F("[ERROR] #{doc} - VShip notification lookup failed, nothing sent\n{err}\n")` [failed].
The plan summary (10-pipeline.md) lists every row that took the `send` default so a human sees it before confirming.

### 6.3 PAID_UPDATE (in window, invoice fully paid)

Original `process_invoice` paid branch: set the ETA custom field and save — **no e-mail, no DocNumber
change, no VShip note**; then look up the VShip booking id and PATCH its expected-arrival date.
Actions, in order:
1. QBO: `update_invoice(inv, eta=eta.date())`
2. VShip: `patch_expected_arrival(vship_booking_id, eta)`

### 6.4 NOTIFY (in window, not fully paid, not routed to Accounting)

Actions, in order:
1. `subject = subject_for(inv.doc_number, eta, notif_sent=(notif.count == 1), paid=False, now=run_now)` — uses the
   DocNumber **before** any change (§8).
2. `new_doc = with_arrival_suffix(inv.doc_number) if eta.date() <= today else None` (§9).
3. QBO: `inv2 = update_invoice(inv, eta=eta.date(), doc_number=new_doc)`.
4. QBO: `send_invoice(inv2, subject=subject)`.
   **D11:** if step 4 fails and step 3 changed the DocNumber, revert it (`update_invoice(inv2', doc_number=inv.doc_number)`,
   best effort) so the next run sees the invoice under its old number; mention the revert outcome in the failure entry.
5. VShip: post comment `vship_comment_for(eta, notif_index=(1 if notif.count == 1 else 0), now=run_now)` (§10).
6. VShip: `patch_expected_arrival(vship_booking_id, eta)`.

### 6.5 FUTURE_UPDATE (outside window)

1. QBO: `update_invoice(inv, eta=eta.date())`
2. VShip: post comment `vship_comment_for(eta, notif_index=0, now=run_now)` → always `ARRIVING ON mm/dd.` here
3. VShip: `patch_expected_arrival(vship_booking_id, eta)`

### 6.6 Failure handling inside PAID_UPDATE / NOTIFY / FUTURE_UPDATE

Steps run in order; the first failure stops the remaining steps of that row.

| Failing step | Entry | Counter |
|---|---|---|
| any QBO step (lookup aside), or the TR/SWB lookup | `[ERROR] #{doc} - QB Invoice Processing Error, No Email Sent\n{err}\n` | failed |
| resolving the VShip booking id or posting the comment (after QBO succeeded) | `[ERROR] #{doc} - Note Write Error, QB Invoice Processing Successful\n{err}\n` | failed |
| PATCH of the VShip ETA (after everything else succeeded) | `[ERROR] #{doc} - Booking ETA Change Failed, QB Invoice Processing Successful\n{err}\n` | failed (**D12**: original counted it as neither ok nor failed) |
| all steps succeeded | log `[OK]    #{doc}` | ok |

**D13 (message unification):** the original used slightly different texts in the out-of-window branch
("Note Write Error, Email Still Sent" although no e-mail is sent there; "QB Invoice Processing Error, QB NOT
Saved"); the new program uses the three texts above everywhere so they can be grepped reliably.

### 6.7 ACCOUNTING routing detail

Only evaluated when the invoice is not fully paid **and** `is_partially_paid` (04-quickbooks-online.md
defines both properties to match the QBO UI). TR/SWB is checked on the VShip **internal comments** of the
base booking (§12). If the TR/SWB lookup itself fails → §6.6 first row (QB Invoice Processing Error, No Email
Sent) — parity: in the original the exception escaped `process_invoice`.

## 7. Routes without carrier lookup

### 7.1 MALFORMED
Entry (reproduce the original dict repr exactly):
```
[ERROR] Row {'inv_number': '<doc_number>', 'amount_due': '<amount_raw>'} - Malformed row (missing amount column or non-numeric amount).
<error text>
```
followed by a blank line (the template ends with `\n` and the writer adds `\n`). `<error text>` is
`could not convert string to float: '<cleaned amount>'` for parity with the original's `float()` message.

### 7.2 BINDU (amount below threshold)
`Send2Bindu.csv` row `[doc_number, amount_raw, customer_name]` via `csv.writer`.
`customer_name` = VShip booking `customerName` for the base booking. **D14:** if the lookup fails, write
`""` and log a WARNING (the original crashed the whole run). Not counted as ok or failed ("routed").

### 7.3 BEN
`Send2Ben.txt` line `doc_number`. Routed.

### 7.4 ACCOUNTING
`Send2Accounting.txt` line `f"{doc_number} - is partially paid and has a TR/SWB note"`. Routed.

## 8. E-mail subject (`texts.subject_for`)

```python
def subject_for(doc_number: str, eta: datetime, *, notif_sent: bool, paid: bool, now: datetime) -> str:
    d = eta.strftime("%m/%d")
    p = f"Invoice for Booking no. {doc_number}."
    arrived, estimated = eta <= now, eta >= now
    if notif_sent:
        if arrived and paid:       return f"{p} ****ARRIVED ON {d}. PLEASE CLEAR THE CARGO****"
        if arrived and not paid:   return f"{p} ****ARRIVED ON {d}. PLEASE PAY AND CLEAR THIS PAST DUE INVOICE AND CLEAR THE CARGO****"
        if estimated and paid:     return f"{p} ***ESTIMATED ARRIVING ON {d}.****"
        if estimated and not paid: return f"{p} ***ESTIMATED ARRIVING ON {d}. PLEASE MAKE PAYMENT ARRANGEMENT****"
        return f"{p} ***Please Check Attached Invoice for ETA***"
    else:
        if arrived and paid:       return f"{p} ****ARRIVED ON {d}. PLEASE CLEAR THE CARGO****"
        if arrived and not paid:   return f"{p} ****ARRIVED ON {d}. PLEASE PLEASE PAY AND CLEAR THE CARGO****"
        if estimated and paid:     return f"{p} ***ESTIMATED ARRIVING ON {d}.****"
        if estimated and not paid: return f"{p} ***ESTIMATED ARRIVING ON {d}. PLEASE MAKE PAYMENT ARRANGEMENT****"
        return f"{p} ***Please Check Attached Invoice for ETA***"
```

Golden outputs captured from the original function (doc `EBKG12345678`, past ETA 11/03, future ETA 11/08):

| notif_sent | paid | ETA | Subject |
|---|---|---|---|
| False | False | past | `Invoice for Booking no. EBKG12345678. ****ARRIVED ON 11/03. PLEASE PLEASE PAY AND CLEAR THE CARGO****` |
| False | False | future | `Invoice for Booking no. EBKG12345678. ***ESTIMATED ARRIVING ON 11/08. PLEASE MAKE PAYMENT ARRANGEMENT****` |
| False | True | past | `Invoice for Booking no. EBKG12345678. ****ARRIVED ON 11/03. PLEASE CLEAR THE CARGO****` |
| False | True | future | `Invoice for Booking no. EBKG12345678. ***ESTIMATED ARRIVING ON 11/08.****` |
| True | False | past | `Invoice for Booking no. EBKG12345678. ****ARRIVED ON 11/03. PLEASE PAY AND CLEAR THIS PAST DUE INVOICE AND CLEAR THE CARGO****` |
| True | False | future | `Invoice for Booking no. EBKG12345678. ***ESTIMATED ARRIVING ON 11/08. PLEASE MAKE PAYMENT ARRANGEMENT****` |
| True | True | past | `Invoice for Booking no. EBKG12345678. ****ARRIVED ON 11/03. PLEASE CLEAR THE CARGO****` |
| True | True | future | `Invoice for Booking no. EBKG12345678. ***ESTIMATED ARRIVING ON 11/08.****` |

In practice `paid` is always `False` when a subject is built (paid invoices take PAID_UPDATE), so only the
four `paid=False` strings are ever sent. `notif_sent` is `True` exactly when the VShip notif status count is 1.
Strings are byte-for-byte; do not "fix" `PLEASE PLEASE` (O3) or the asterisk counts.

## 9. DocNumber arrival suffix (`rules.with_arrival_suffix`)

```python
def with_arrival_suffix(doc_number: str) -> str:
    return doc_number + (" A" if doc_number[-1].isdigit() else "A")
```
Applied only in NOTIFY and only when `eta.date() <= today`.
`EBKG12345678` → `EBKG12345678 A`; `EBKG12345678 A` → `EBKG12345678 AA`; `267546627` → `267546627 A`.
If the result exceeds the QBO DocNumber length limit (see 04), do not truncate — fail the row with
`QB Invoice Processing Error, No Email Sent` and the reason.

## 10. VShip note text (`texts.vship_comment_for`)

```python
def vship_comment_for(eta: datetime, *, notif_index: int, now: datetime) -> str:
    if eta < now:
        return f"ARRIVED ON {eta.strftime('%m/%d')}. NOTIF #{notif_index + 1}"
    return f"ARRIVING ON {eta.strftime('%m/%d')}."
```
Examples: arrived 11/03, first notice → `ARRIVED ON 11/03. NOTIF #1`; second → `ARRIVED ON 11/03. NOTIF #2`;
future 11/18 → `ARRIVING ON 11/18.`. Posted with `commentType: 1` (05-vship-crm.md).

## 11. Notification status (`vship/logic.notif_status`)

Input: the booking's `internalComments` list (05-vship-crm.md) and `run_now`.

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NotifStatus:
    count: int          # 0, 1 or 2
    have_to_do: bool

def notif_status(comments: list[dict], run_now: datetime) -> NotifStatus:
    texts = [(c.get("comment") or "") for c in comments]
    n1 = [c for c in comments if "notif #1" in (c.get("comment") or "").lower()]
    if not n1:
        return NotifStatus(0, True)
    if any("notif #2" in t.lower() for t in texts):
        return NotifStatus(2, False)
    newest = max(parse_vship_datetime(c.get("createdDate")) for c in n1)      # D15
    return NotifStatus(1, not (newest > run_now - timedelta(days=7)))
```
- `"notif #2"` alone without `"notif #1"` → count 0 (parity: the original only checks #2 after finding #1).
- **D15:** the original used the createdDate of the *first* `notif #1` comment in API order; the new code uses
  the *most recent* one (intent: "done in the last week"). Identical when there is one such comment.
- `parse_vship_datetime`: ISO-8601; aware → converted to local time then made naive; naive → as-is;
  unparseable → treat as "old" (have_to_do=True) and log a WARNING.
- A missing/`null` `internalComments` is treated as `[]` (the original raised and fell into §6.2).

## 12. TR/SWB note detection (`vship/logic.has_tr_swb_note`)

Port verbatim (lists include the original's duplicate `"PR FOR TR"`):

```python
KEYWORDS = ["PAID IN FULL, TR FEE SENT TO MSC FOR TR", "PR FOR TR", "PS FOR TR", "PR FOR TR", "PS FOR RTR",
            "PR/ PS FOR TR", "RTR", "SWB RCVD", "TR RECVD", "TR RCVD"]
EXCLUDE  = ["PS - LESS TR FEE, ", "NO TR", "TR PENDING"]

def _build_pattern(words):
    return re.compile(r"\b(?:" + "|".join(re.escape(kw) for kw in words) + r")\b", re.IGNORECASE)

_PATTERN = _build_pattern(KEYWORDS)
_EXCLUDE = _build_pattern(EXCLUDE)

def is_tr_swb_comment(text: str) -> bool:
    return bool(_PATTERN.search(_EXCLUDE.sub("", text)))

def has_tr_swb_note(comments: list[dict]) -> bool:
    return any(is_tr_swb_comment(c.get("comment") or "") for c in comments)
```

Golden cases (from the original code):

| Comment | Match |
|---|---|
| `SWB RCVD 10/12` | True |
| `swb rcvd` | True |
| `TR RCVD` | True |
| `TR RECVD BY JOHN` | True |
| `RTR` / `RTR SENT` | True |
| `PR FOR TR` / `PR/ PS FOR TR` / `PS FOR RTR` | True |
| `PAID IN FULL, TR FEE SENT TO MSC FOR TR` | True |
| `NO TR` / `TR PENDING` | False |
| `NO TR - SWB RCVD` | True |
| `TR PENDING, RTR` | True |
| `PS - LESS TR FEE, PAID` | False |
| `PS - LESS TR FEE, RTR` | True |
| `STRTR` / `TR RCVDX` / `SWBRCVD` | False |
| `PR FOR TRUCKING` | False |
| `ARRIVED ON 11/02. NOTIF #1` | False |

## 13. Counters and summary

- `ok`: rows whose PAID_UPDATE / NOTIFY / FUTURE_UPDATE completed every step.
- `failed`: every row that wrote to Failed_To_Process.txt or PotentialCustomsHold.txt.
- `routed`: BINDU, BEN, ACCOUNTING. `skipped`: SKIP_R.
- Final line (parity): `Done: {ok} succeeded, {failed} failed/skipped.` followed by a per-route breakdown table
  (10-pipeline.md).

## 14. Output files and exact entry templates

All files live in `ETA_OUTPUT_DIR` (default: the current working directory, like the original), are opened
in **append** mode with UTF-8 encoding, and each `write` appends `entry + "\n"`.

| File | Entry |
|---|---|
| `Send2Bindu.csv` | CSV row `[doc_number, amount_raw, customer_name]` (`newline=""`; write a UTF-8 BOM only when creating the file) |
| `Send2Ben.txt` | `{doc_number}` |
| `Send2Accounting.txt` | `{doc_number} - is partially paid and has a TR/SWB note` |
| `PotentialCustomsHold.txt` | `[ERROR] #{doc_number} -  Possible Customs Hold.` |
| `Failed_To_Process.txt` | one of the templates below |

Failed_To_Process.txt templates (`{err}` = `str(exception)`):

```
[ERROR] Row {'inv_number': '...', 'amount_due': '...'} - Malformed row (missing amount column or non-numeric amount).\n{err}\n
{doc_number}                                                      ← MANUAL rows
[ERROR] #{doc} - Carrier Lookup Failed.\n{err}\n
[ERROR] #{doc} -  Can't determine ETA.\n{err}\n
[ERROR] #{doc} - Unexpected error during carrier lookup.\n{err}\n
[ERROR] #{doc} - VShip notification lookup failed, nothing sent\n{err}\n     ← only with ETA_ON_NOTIF_LOOKUP_ERROR=fail
[SKIP] #{doc} - Done in the last week
[SKIP] #{doc} - not found in QuickBooks
[SKIP] #{doc} - duplicate row in input file (line {n})
[ERROR] #{doc} - QB Invoice Processing Error, No Email Sent\n{err}\n
[ERROR] #{doc} - Note Write Error, QB Invoice Processing Successful\n{err}\n
[ERROR] #{doc} - Booking ETA Change Failed, QB Invoice Processing Successful\n{err}\n
[SKIP] #{doc} - already e-mailed today at {HH:MM} (ledger); use --force to resend      ← 10-pipeline.md
```

In dry-run mode none of these files is written (10-pipeline.md); the plan report shows what would be written.

## 15. Deliberate deviations from the original (review list)

| # | Original behaviour | New behaviour | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Empty DocNumber crashed the run | MALFORMED row | Robustness |
| D2 | Header row reported as malformed | First-row header skipped silently | Noise |
| D3 | Duplicate rows processed twice | First occurrence only | Avoid double e-mails |
| D4 | 1-char `a` row silently ignored | MANUAL (reported) | Visibility |
| D5 | Carrier patterns case-sensitive | Base booking upper-cased first | Harmless |
| D6 | Extra text sent to carrier | Clear CarrierLookupError | Same outcome, clearer |
| D7 | Ref pattern `2026\d{6}` | `20\d{8}` | Year-proof |
| D8 | NOTIF1_SENT rows "not have-to-do" logged as "not found in QuickBooks" | "Done in the last week" | Copy-paste bug |
| D9 | Out-of-window row missing in QBO silently skipped | Reported as not found | Visibility |
| D10 | "ETA not found" path | Merged into "Can't determine ETA." | Single contract |
| D11 | DocNumber stays changed if send fails | Best-effort revert | Keeps state consistent |
| D12 | VShip ETA PATCH failure counted as nothing | Counted as failed | Accurate summary |
| D13 | Inconsistent/misleading failure texts | Three unified texts | Greppable |
| D14 | Customer-name failure crashed the run | Empty name + WARNING | Robustness |
| D15 | First `notif #1` comment's date | Most recent `notif #1` date | Matches intent |
| D16 | TR/SWB + VShip lookups for STANDARD rows used `doc[:-1]` (last digit chopped) and NOTIF1_SENT paid rows searched VShip with the suffix still attached | Base booking everywhere | Bug fix |
| D17 | VShip best-match accepted unrelated bookings | Must be exact/prefix/contains match (05 §6) | Avoid editing the wrong booking |
| D18 | Several VShip searches per row | One cached lookup per base booking per run | Speed |
| D19 | Single per-run timestamp not used | `run_now` captured once | Consistency |
| D20 | No confirmation, no dry-run, no ledger | plan → confirm → apply, `--dry-run`, same-day e-mail ledger | Safety (sends customer e-mail) |
| D21 | Several QBO invoices with the same DocNumber → the first one was used | Not processed; `QB Invoice Processing Error, No Email Sent` + the list of invoice Ids (04 §6.3) | Never e-mail from an arbitrary duplicate |
| D22 | UI always clicked Save | An update whose values already match is skipped (no API call) | Same result, fewer calls |

Integration specs add carrier-specific deviations with their own labels (e.g. `CMA-D1…D6` in 08,
Maersk's in 07 §7.6); they follow the same rule: isolated, commented, listed in the spec.

If the user wants strict parity for any item, it is a one-line change in `rules.py`/`pipeline.py`; keep each
deviation isolated and commented with its D-number.

## 16. Quirks intentionally preserved

| # | Quirk |
|---|---|
| O1 | Carrier-local ETA wall time compared with machine-local `run_now` (no tz conversion), as the original did. |
| O2 | Two spaces in `-  Can't determine ETA.` and `-  Possible Customs Hold.` |
| O3 | Subject text `PLEASE PLEASE PAY AND CLEAR THE CARGO` for the first arrival notice. |
| O4 | Pre-arrival in-window invoices are e-mailed on every run until arrival (no cooldown). |
| O5 | Every out-of-window run posts a fresh `ARRIVING ON mm/dd.` VShip note. |
| O6 | Boundary inconsistency: an ETA later today gets the DocNumber `A` (date rule) while the subject says "ESTIMATED ARRIVING" and the note says "ARRIVING". |
| O7 | `notif #2` without `notif #1` counts as 0. |
| O8 | MSC uses only the first container's events (06-carrier-msc.md). |

# 02 — Configuration, secrets and local state

All configuration comes from environment variables, normally via a `.env` file in the working directory
(`load_dotenv(..., override=True)` — `.env` wins over OS variables, as in the original). `.env` must be
git-ignored. The implementer generates `.env.example` from the tables below (every variable, with the
default or a placeholder and a one-line comment).

## 1. Run settings (`RunSettings`)

| Env var | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ETA_OUTPUT_DIR` | current working directory | Where `Send2Bindu.csv`, `Send2Ben.txt`, `Send2Accounting.txt`, `Failed_To_Process.txt`, `PotentialCustomsHold.txt` are appended (same names as the original), plus `reports/` and `logs/` |
| `ETA_STATE_DIR` | Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ETAutomationsAPI`; else `$XDG_STATE_HOME/eta_automations` or `~/.local/state/eta_automations` | `tokens.json`, `ledger.jsonl`, `probe/`, e-mail recovery file (04). Created with user-only permissions |
| `ETA_MIN_INVOICE_AMOUNT` | `1000` | Rows below this amount go to Send2Bindu.csv (01 §3) |
| `ETA_WINDOW_BUSINESS_DAYS` | `6` | Business-day window (01 §5) |
| `ETA_ON_NOTIF_LOOKUP_ERROR` | `send` | `send` (parity) or `fail` (01 §6.2) |
| `ETA_MAX_PARALLEL_BOOKINGS` | `8` | Rows processed concurrently (10 §4) |
| `ETA_CARRIER_FAILURE_LIMIT` | `5` | Consecutive carrier failures before the circuit breaker trips (10 §6) |
| `ETA_LOG_LEVEL` | `INFO` | Console log level |
| `ETA_PROVIDER_MSC` / `ETA_PROVIDER_MAERSK` / `ETA_PROVIDER_CMA` / `ETA_PROVIDER_GRIMALDI` | `native` / `native` / `native` / `off` | Which client serves each carrier: `native`, `aggregator`, `off` (09) |

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RunSettings:
    output_dir: Path
    state_dir: Path
    min_invoice_amount: Decimal = Decimal("1000")
    window_business_days: int = 6
    on_notif_lookup_error: Literal["send", "fail"] = "send"
    max_parallel_bookings: int = 8
    carrier_failure_limit: int = 5
    log_level: str = "INFO"
    providers: Mapping[Carrier, Literal["native", "aggregator", "off"]] = ...
```

| `AGG_ALLOW_CREATE` | no | `true` (`false` = never spend credits) |
| `AGG_MAX_CREATES_PER_RUN` | no | `100` |

| `AGG_SCAC_MSC` / `AGG_SCAC_MAERSK` / `AGG_SCAC_CMA` / `AGG_SCAC_GRIMALDI` | no | `MSCU` / `MAEU` / `CMDU` / `GRIU` |

### 2.7 Company-mailbox e-mail (only for `QB_EMAIL_STRATEGY=graph` or `smtp`) — see 04b §3

| Env var | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `EMAIL_FROM` | yes | — (sending mailbox) |

## 3. Obsolete variables from the original

| Variable | Why it is gone |
|---|---|
| `QB` | QBO web-login password — no browser login any more |
| `QB_HEADLESS` | No browser |
| `HOME_PAGE` | MSC browser navigation target |
| `LOGIN_URL`, `MSC_PASSWORD` | MSC browser sign-in — not automated any more (06 §1); the official API key or a pasted token replaces them |

Unknown variables are ignored (log obsolete ones once at INFO/DEBUG as the specs say).

## 4. Local state files (`ETA_STATE_DIR`)

| File | Content | Sensitive |
|---|---|---|
| `tokens.json` | Access tokens + QBO refresh token (03 §7) | **yes** (0600) |
| `ledger.jsonl` | Completed write actions (10 §9) | low |
| `run.lock` | Single-instance OS lock (03 §14) | no |
| `probe/*.json` | Redacted raw payloads from `eta probe` | low (redacted) |
| `qbo_email_template_recovery.json` | Original QBO e-mail subject while a template swap is in flight (04b §6.2) | low |
| `qbo_email_probe.json` | Human-confirmed e-mail verification records (04b §10) | low |
| `aggregator_tracking.json` | Aggregator tracking-request ids (09), if used | low |

None of these may be inside the git repository. On first run, the program migrates nothing from the old
tool (the old token files are browser sessions and are not reusable); the only value to carry over is
`QB_REFRESH_TOKEN` (and the other credentials in the old `.env`).

## 5. Secrets handling rules

- Secrets live only in `.env` and `tokens.json`. Never in logs, reports, exceptions, probe files or the ledger.
- `.env` write-back is limited to `QB_REFRESH_TOKEN` (04) and uses `dotenv.set_key(env_path, "QB_REFRESH_TOKEN", value)`
  — never rewrite the whole file.
- The repository's `.gitignore` already lists `.env`, `*.log`, `reports/`, `logs/`, `Send2*.txt`,
  `Send2Bindu.csv`, `Failed_To_Process.txt`, `PotentialCustomsHold.txt`, `ToEmail_*.csv`; keep it. Unlike the
  original, it must **not** ignore `*.json` — the test fixtures are JSON files.

# 03 — Foundations: shared contracts every module uses

This file is the **single source of truth** for package layout, shared types,
error classes, the HTTP layer, token caching, the carrier interface, logging and
settings conventions. Every other spec file uses the names defined here. If
another file appears to contradict this one, **this file wins** unless the
other file explicitly says "overrides 03-foundations §X".

---

## 1. Project layout (src layout, Python ≥ 3.12)

```
pyproject.toml
README.md                      # end-user README for the program (see 11-cli.md §8)
.env.example                   # generated from 02-configuration.md
src/eta_automations/
  __init__.py                  # __version__ = "1.0.0"
  __main__.py                  # `python -m eta_automations` → cli.main()
  cli.py                       # argparse CLI (11-cli.md)
  config.py                    # Settings + load_settings() (02-configuration.md)
  clock.py                     # Clock / SystemClock / FixedClock (§3)
  models.py                    # Carrier, EtaResult (§4) + pipeline models (10-pipeline.md)
  errors.py                    # exception hierarchy (§5)
  http.py                      # httpx client factory, request(), retries, rate limiter (§6)
  token_store.py               # TokenStore (§7)
  auth.py                      # TokenProvider protocol + request_with_auth() (§8)
  logging_setup.py             # logging config + redact() (§11)
  business_days.py             # 6-business-day window (01-business-rules.md §4)
  rules.py                     # pure decision functions (01-business-rules.md)
  texts.py                     # email subject + VShip note text (01-business-rules.md §7–8)
  outputs.py                   # Send2*.txt / Failed_To_Process.txt writers (10-pipeline.md)
  ledger.py                    # idempotency ledger (10-pipeline.md)
  run_lock.py                  # single-instance OS file lock (§14)
  pipeline.py                  # plan → confirm → apply orchestration (10-pipeline.md)
  qbo/
    __init__.py
    auth.py                    # OAuth2 refresh-token flow (04-quickbooks-online.md)
    client.py                  # QboClient (04-quickbooks-online.md)
    email.py                   # invoice e-mail delivery strategy (04-quickbooks-online.md)
  vship/
    __init__.py
    client.py                  # VShipClient (05-vship-crm.md)
    logic.py                   # notif status, TR/SWB matcher, booking best-match (05-vship-crm.md)
  carriers/
    __init__.py
    base.py                    # CarrierClient protocol (§9)
    router.py                  # booking number → Carrier (01-business-rules.md §3)
    dcsa.py                    # shared DCSA Track & Trace parser (09-dcsa-aggregators-grimaldi.md)
    msc.py                     # (06-carrier-msc.md)

    cma.py                     # (08-carrier-cma-cgm.md)

tests/

  fixtures/<service>/*.json    # sample payloads given in the spec files
  test_*.py                    # see 12-testing.md
```

Rules:
- No browser automation of any kind (no Playwright, Selenium, Puppeteer,
  pyppeteer, undetected-chromedriver, requests-html JS rendering, etc.).
- No module performs network I/O at import time. No module reads `.env` at
  import time — only `config.load_settings()` does, called once by the CLI.
- Everything that talks to the network is `async` and uses `httpx.AsyncClient`.

## 2. Dependencies (`pyproject.toml`)

Runtime (minimum versions; do not pin exact patch versions):

| Package | Why |
|---|---|
| `httpx>=0.28,<1` | All HTTP (async). |
| `python-dotenv>=1.0` | `.env` loading and writing back rotated values. |
| `pandas>=2.2` | Only for `CustomBusinessDay` + `USFederalHolidayCalendar` in `business_days.py` (exact parity with the original). Import it lazily inside that module. |
| `tzdata>=2024.1` | IANA time-zone data for `zoneinfo` (Windows has none built in); used by `dcsa.to_local_naive()` (09 §A.3.3). |

Optional extras (declared as `[project.optional-dependencies]`): any extra an
integration spec asks for (e.g. an e-mail backend in 04). Code must import
optional packages lazily and raise `ConfigError` with an install hint when the
feature is enabled but the package is missing.

Dev extras (`dev`): `pytest>=8`, `pytest-asyncio>=0.24`, `respx>=0.22`.
`pytest-asyncio` runs in `asyncio_mode = "auto"` (set in `pyproject.toml`).

Entry point: `[project.scripts] eta = "eta_automations.cli:main"`.

## 3. Clock (`clock.py`)

```python
class Clock(Protocol):
    def now(self) -> datetime: ...          # naive local wall-clock time

class SystemClock:                           # now() -> datetime.now()
class FixedClock:                            # FixedClock(datetime(2026, 11, 5, 9, 30)).now() -> that value
```

The pipeline captures `run_now = clock.now()` **once** at the start of a run
and uses that single value for every time comparison in the run (window
cutoff, "has it arrived", "Notif #1 within 7 days", MSC transshipment rule).
`today = run_now.date()`. Nothing else in the code calls `datetime.now()`
except `SystemClock` and log/report timestamps.

## 4. Shared models (`models.py`)

```python
class Carrier(StrEnum):
    MSC = "MSC"
    MAERSK = "Maersk"
    CMA = "CMA"
    GRIMALDI = "Grimaldi"

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class EtaResult:
    carrier: Carrier
    booking: str                 # the base booking number that was queried (no suffixes)
    eta: datetime                # NAIVE datetime: carrier-reported local wall-clock time at the
                                 # port/terminal (any tz offset is parsed, then DROPPED, keeping the
                                 # local wall time — this is what the carrier website displays and
                                 # what the original code compared against). Date-only sources use 00:00.
    source: str                  # short human description, e.g. "MSC event 'Estimated Time of Arrival'",
                                 # "DCSA TRANSPORT ARRI/EST at USSAV"
    is_actual: bool = False      # True when the source says the arrival/discharge already happened
    from_transshipment_rule: bool = False   # MSC fallback rule used (06-carrier-msc.md)
    containers: tuple[str, ...] = ()        # container numbers considered, if known
    details: Mapping[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)  # small JSON-serializable extras for the report
```

Pipeline-specific models (`InputRow`, `ParsedBooking`, `Route`, `Plan`,
`Action`, …) are defined in `10-pipeline.md`.

## 5. Errors (`errors.py`)

```python
class EtaAutomationError(Exception): ...            # base for everything below

class ConfigError(EtaAutomationError): ...          # missing/invalid settings, missing optional package
class AuthError(EtaAutomationError): ...            # credentials rejected / token unobtainable

class ServiceError(EtaAutomationError):
    """Unexpected HTTP status or malformed payload from an external service."""
    def __init__(self, service: str, message: str, *, status: int | None = None,
                 body_excerpt: str = "", request_id: str | None = None): ...
    # str(err) -> f"{service}: {message} (HTTP {status}) [request_id=...] body: {excerpt}"
    # body_excerpt is <= 500 chars and already passed through redact()

# ── carriers ──
class CarrierLookupError(EtaAutomationError): ...   # lookup failed: network, blocked, not found at carrier,
                                                    # carrier not configured → "Carrier Lookup Failed."
class UnsupportedCarrierError(CarrierLookupError): ...  # Grimaldi stub, reference numbers, unknown pattern
class AggregatorBookingError(CarrierLookupError): ...   # per-booking aggregator state, e.g. "not tracked yet — re-run later"
                                                        # (09 §B.7.1 describes it; define it HERE and import it in aggregator.py)
class NoEtaError(EtaAutomationError): ...           # booking found but no usable ETA → "Can't determine ETA."
class CustomsHoldError(EtaAutomationError): ...     # MSC heuristic → PotentialCustomsHold.txt

# ── VShip ──
class VShipBookingNotFoundError(ServiceError): ...
class NoteError(ServiceError): ...                  # posting a VShip comment failed
class BookingChangeError(ServiceError): ...         # PATCHing the VShip booking ETA failed

# ── QuickBooks ──
class InvoiceNotFoundError(EtaAutomationError): ...
class AmbiguousInvoiceError(InvoiceNotFoundError): ...     # several invoices share one DocNumber (04 §6.3)
class InvoiceUpdateError(ServiceError): ...
class InvoiceSendError(ServiceError): ...
class EmailPathUnavailableError(InvoiceSendError): ...     # no invoice e-mail can be sent this run (04b §6.1)
class TemplateRestoreError(EmailPathUnavailableError): ... # QBO e-mail template left modified (04b §6.2)

# ── single-instance guard ──
class RunLockedError(EtaAutomationError): ...              # another instance holds the run lock (§14)

# ── business routing signal (not a failure) ──
class SWBTRError(EtaAutomationError): ...           # partially paid + TR/SWB note → Send2Accounting.txt
                                                    # (kept for parity/readability; the new pipeline decides the
                                                    # ACCOUNTING route while planning and need not raise it)
```

**Carrier boundary rule:** `CarrierClient.get_eta()` may raise **only**
`CarrierLookupError` (or a subclass), `NoEtaError`, or `CustomsHoldError`.
Carrier clients must catch `ServiceError`, `AuthError`, `httpx.HTTPError`,
`KeyError`/`TypeError`/`ValueError` from parsing, etc. and re-raise them as
`CarrierLookupError(...)` (or `NoEtaError` when the payload is valid but has no
usable date), chaining with `raise ... from exc`. Anything else escaping
`get_eta()` is a bug; the pipeline still catches it and records
"Unexpected error during carrier lookup." (parity with the original).

## 6. HTTP layer (`http.py`)

```python
DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = httpx.Timeout(30.0, connect=10.0)

def new_async_client(*, base_url: str = "", headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
                     timeout: httpx.Timeout | float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT) -> httpx.AsyncClient:
    """follow_redirects=False, trust_env=True (honours HTTPS_PROXY / SSL_CERT_FILE),
    default headers: {"User-Agent": f"ETAutomationsAPI/{__version__}", "Accept": "application/json"}
    merged with `headers`."""

async def request(client: httpx.AsyncClient, method: str, url: str, *, service: str,
                  expected: Collection[int] = (200,), idempotent: bool | None = None,
                  max_attempts: int = 4, limiter: "AsyncLimiter | None" = None,
                  **kwargs) -> httpx.Response:
    ...

def json_body(resp: httpx.Response, *, service: str) -> Any:
    """resp.json() or raise ServiceError(service, 'response was not valid JSON', status=..., body_excerpt=...)."""
```

`request()` behaviour:
1. `idempotent` defaults to `True` for GET/HEAD/OPTIONS/PUT/DELETE and `False` for POST/PATCH.
   Callers may pass `idempotent=True` for POSTs that are pure reads (e.g. GraphQL queries, QBO query endpoint, OAuth token calls).
2. Attempt loop (`max_attempts` total). Retry when:
   - `httpx.ConnectError`, `httpx.ConnectTimeout`, `httpx.PoolTimeout` — always (request never reached the server);
   - `httpx.ReadTimeout`, `httpx.WriteTimeout`, `httpx.RemoteProtocolError` — only if idempotent;
   - status `429` or `503` — always (server explicitly refused, nothing was processed);
   - status `500`, `502`, `504` — only if idempotent.
   Backoff before attempt *n* (n ≥ 2): `min(30, 0.5 * 2**(n-2)) + random.uniform(0, 0.25)` seconds,
   or the `Retry-After` header value (seconds or HTTP-date) if present, capped at 30 s.
3. If the final status is in `expected` → return the response.
4. Otherwise raise `ServiceError(service, f"unexpected HTTP {status} for {method} {redacted_path}", status=..., body_excerpt=redact(resp.text)[:500], request_id=<first present of headers 'intuit_tid', 'x-request-id', 'x-correlation-id', 'x-correlationid', 'x-kong-request-id', 'x-azure-ref', 'request-id'>)`.
   **401 and 403 are never retried here** — see `request_with_auth()` in §8.
5. Transport errors that exhaust the attempts are re-raised as
   `ServiceError(service, f"network error: {exc!r}")` chained from the original.
6. Every attempt logs at DEBUG on logger `eta.http`: method, redacted URL, status (or exception), elapsed ms, attempt number.
7. If `limiter` is given, `async with limiter:` wraps each attempt (see §10).

## 7. Token store (`token_store.py`)

```python
class TokenStore:
    def __init__(self, path: Path): ...                  # e.g. <ETA_STATE_DIR>/tokens.json
    def get(self, key: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None: ...
    def put(self, key: str, value: dict[str, Any]) -> None: ...   # atomic: write tmp file in same dir,
                                                                  # flush+fsync, os.replace; chmod 0o600 on POSIX
    def delete(self, key: str) -> None: ...

def is_fresh(entry: Mapping[str, Any] | None, *, skew_seconds: int = 120, now: float | None = None) -> bool:
    """True if entry has 'access_token' and 'expires_at' (epoch seconds) > now + skew."""

def jwt_exp(token: str) -> float | None:
    """If `token` looks like a JWT (three dot-separated segments), base64url-decode the payload segment
    (padding added as needed, NO signature verification) and return its numeric `exp` claim as epoch
    seconds; otherwise, or on any decoding error, return None. Shared by every auth provider."""
```

- One JSON object, top-level keys = service names: `"qbo"`, `"vship"`, `"msc"`, `"maersk"`, `"cma"`, `"aggregator"`, …
- Each value has at least `access_token: str` and `expires_at: float` (Unix epoch seconds). Services may add
  keys (e.g. QBO stores `refresh_token`, `refresh_token_expires_at`, `refresh_token_seed`).
- Corrupt/unreadable file → log a WARNING, treat as empty, and overwrite on next `put()`.
- Guard reads/writes with a `threading.Lock` (writes are synchronous and tiny).
- When a JWT is received and no explicit lifetime is given, derive `expires_at` from the JWT `exp` claim
  (base64url-decode the payload segment; **no signature verification**); if that fails, use the
  service-specific default lifetime documented in that service's spec.

## 8. Auth pattern (`auth.py`)

```python
class TokenProvider(Protocol):
    async def get_token(self) -> str: ...      # cached-if-fresh, else obtain/refresh (under an asyncio.Lock)
    async def invalidate(self) -> None: ...    # drop the cached access token (keep refresh tokens)

async def request_with_auth(client: httpx.AsyncClient, method: str, url: str, *, service: str,
                            auth: TokenProvider,
                            build_headers: Callable[[str], Mapping[str, str]] = lambda t: {"Authorization": f"Bearer {t}"},
                            **kwargs) -> httpx.Response:
    """token = await auth.get_token(); call request(...) with merged headers.
    If it raises ServiceError with status 401 (or 403 when the service spec says 403 means 'token expired'):
    await auth.invalidate(); get a fresh token; retry exactly once. A second 401/403 raises
    AuthError(f"{service}: credentials/token rejected (HTTP {status})")."""
```

Each service implements its own `TokenProvider` (`QboAuth`, `VShipAuth`, `MscAuth`, `MaerskAuth`, …).
Concurrency rule: `get_token()` takes an `asyncio.Lock`, re-checks freshness inside the lock, and only
then performs the network call — so 20 concurrent coroutines trigger one login, not 20.
**A token provider never acquires its service's concurrency semaphore** (§10): callers may already hold a
slot while awaiting the token, so acquiring it again could deadlock. Token calls go straight through
`http.request()`.

## 9. Carrier client contract (`carriers/base.py`)

```python
class CarrierClient(Protocol):
    carrier: Carrier
    async def get_eta(self, booking: str) -> EtaResult: ...
        # `booking` is the BASE booking number (suffixes already removed, stripped, upper-cased).
        # Never returns None: raise NoEtaError instead.
        # Raises only CarrierLookupError / NoEtaError / CustomsHoldError (see §5 boundary rule).
    async def probe(self, booking: str) -> dict[str, Any]: ...
        # Diagnostics for the `eta probe <carrier>` command: performs the same calls as get_eta but
        # returns {"requests": [...summaries...], "raw": <payload(s), redacted>, "eta": <EtaResult as dict or error string>}.
    async def aclose(self) -> None: ...
```

Each carrier module exposes a factory:

```python
def build_client(settings: Settings, token_store: TokenStore, *,
                 clock: Clock | None = None, http: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None) -> CarrierClient | None:
    """Return None when the carrier is not configured (required env vars missing).
    `clock` and `http` are passed through to the client constructor: the pipeline passes
    FixedClock(run_now) so every carrier rule uses the run's single timestamp; tests pass a respx-mocked
    client. (Specs 07/08 show the shorter two-argument form — the keyword arguments here are additive.)"""
```

Constructors accept an optional `http: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None` (tests inject a respx-mocked
client) and an optional `clock: Clock`. `carriers/router.py` maps booking numbers to `Carrier`
(01-business-rules.md §3) and holds `dict[Carrier, CarrierClient | None]`; a booking whose carrier
client is `None` fails with `CarrierLookupError(f"{carrier} lookups are not configured — set {vars} in .env")`.

## 10. Concurrency & rate limiting

- One `asyncio.Semaphore` per service, sized from settings (defaults in 02-configuration.md):
  QBO 4, VShip 4, MSC 4, Maersk 3, CMA 2, aggregator 2. A client acquires its semaphore around **each
  HTTP call** (not around a whole booking), so one slow booking never blocks others.
- `http.AsyncLimiter(max_calls: int, period_s: float)` — a small sliding-window limiter usable as
  `async with limiter:`. Use it only where a spec documents a hard per-minute/per-second quota.
- The pipeline's overall fan-out is bounded by `ETA_MAX_PARALLEL_BOOKINGS` (default 8).

## 11. Logging & redaction (`logging_setup.py`)

- `configure_logging(level: str = "INFO", log_file: Path | None = None)`: console handler +
  optional file handler (`<ETA_OUTPUT_DIR>/logs/eta_<YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS>.log`, DEBUG level).
  Format: `"%(asctime)s %(levelname)-7s %(name)s: %(message)s"`, `datefmt="%H:%M:%S"`.
- Logger names: `eta`, `eta.http`, `eta.pipeline`, `eta.qbo`, `eta.vship`, `eta.carrier.msc`,
  `eta.carrier.maersk`, `eta.carrier.cma`, `eta.carrier.dcsa`, `eta.carrier.aggregator`.
- `redact(value)` works on str / Mapping / list (recursively) and returns a redacted copy:
  any key matching `(?i)(authorization|token|secret|password|passwd|cookie|consumer-key|keyid|api[-_]?key|client[-_]?secret|refresh)`
  has its value replaced by `"***"`; in strings, `Bearer <x>` → `Bearer ***`, and URL query parameters
  with those names → `***`. **Never log a secret, token, password or full cookie.**
- Console output must be readable on Windows: the CLI reconfigures `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` to
  UTF-8 with `errors="replace"`.

## 12. Settings access pattern (`config.py`)

`Settings` is a frozen dataclass composed of per-service frozen dataclasses:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Settings:
    run: RunSettings                     # thresholds, dirs, concurrency, providers (02)
    qbo: QboSettings | None              # (04) None when its required vars are missing
    vship: VShipSettings | None          # (05)
    msc: MscSettings | None              # (06)
    maersk: MaerskSettings | None        # (07)
    cma: CmaSettings | None              # (08)
    aggregator: AggregatorSettings | None  # (09)
    email: EmailSettings | None          # (04) only if 04 defines an e-mail backend that needs it
    missing: Mapping[str, tuple[str, ...]]  # service name -> names of its missing required env vars

def require(settings: Settings, *services: str) -> None:
    """Raise ConfigError listing, for every requested service that is None, all of its missing env vars,
    e.g. require(s, "qbo", "vship") at the start of `eta run`."""
```

- `load_settings(env_file: Path | None = None) -> Settings` calls
  `dotenv.load_dotenv(env_file or Path.cwd() / ".env", override=True)` (the original deliberately lets
  `.env` win over OS variables), then reads `os.environ`. It never raises for a missing service; it
  raises `ConfigError` only for **malformed** values (e.g. a non-integer concurrency).
- Each integration spec defines its settings dataclass fields **and** the exact env var names in a
  table (name · required? · default · meaning). 02-configuration.md consolidates them.
- Commands call `require(...)` for what they need: `run` → qbo + vship (+ at least the carriers present
  in the file, checked lazily by the router); `probe qbo` → qbo; `eta eta` → only the carriers involved.
- Booleans accept `1/true/yes/on` and `0/false/no/off` (case-insensitive).

## 13. Conventions for integration spec files (04–09)

Every integration spec uses this outline, in this order:

1. **Summary** — what it replaces in the original code and why it is faster.
2. **Access & onboarding** — accounts/products/keys the user must obtain, who to ask, expected lead time.
3. **Configuration** — settings dataclass + env var table.
4. **Endpoints** — method, URL, headers, params/body, relevant response fields, status codes, errors, rate limits.
5. **Auth / token lifecycle.**
6. **Module design** — file path, classes, exact function signatures with type hints, step-by-step behaviour, error mapping to §5.
7. **Business logic** — ported precisely from the original, with any deviation flagged as **DEVIATION** and justified.
8. **Fallbacks** — honest assessment of alternatives if the primary path is unavailable.
9. **Fixtures & tests** — synthetic sample payloads (in code blocks, each with its `tests/fixtures/...` path) and the list of unit tests.
10. **Probe / verification procedure** — how the user safely confirms it works with real credentials.
11. **Sources & verification status** — table: claim · source URL · status (`VERIFIED-DOCS`, `OBSERVED`, `INFERRED`, `UNVERIFIED`).

Anything not verifiable from public documentation must be marked `UNVERIFIED`, and the code must then be
written defensively (tolerant parsing, clear error messages that include the redacted raw payload keys)
and covered by the probe procedure so the user can confirm it on first run.

## 14. Single-instance run lock (`run_lock.py`)

Two concurrent runs could double-send e-mails and race QuickBooks refresh-token rotation (04 §5.3), so
every command that writes (`run` without `--dry-run`, `qbo-auth`, write probes) holds an exclusive lock:

```python
@contextmanager
def run_lock(state_dir: Path) -> Iterator[None]:
    """Open/create <state_dir>/run.lock and take an exclusive, NON-blocking OS lock on it for the
    lifetime of the process: fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB) on POSIX,
    msvcrt.locking(fd, LK_NBLCK, 1) on Windows (lock byte 0; write a placeholder byte first if the file is empty).
    On contention raise RunLockedError("Another ETAutomationsAPI run is in progress (lock: <path>).").
    Write "pid=<pid> started=<iso time>" into the file for humans; release and close on exit.
    The OS drops the lock automatically if the process dies, so there is no stale-lock handling and
    NO PID probing (on Windows os.kill(pid, 0) would terminate the process)."""
```

Read-only commands (`--dry-run`, `eta eta`, read-only probes) do not take the lock.
