# Part B — `carriers/aggregator.py` (optional third-party provider)

## B.1 Summary

A licensed tracking aggregator gives one API key and one integration for every carrier. Use it:
- while official API approval from Maersk, CMA or MSC is pending;
- if a carrier refuses API access;
- for Grimaldi, which has no public API (Part C).

It replaces the browser lookups with plain HTTPS calls.

**Trade-off:** aggregators are mostly **asynchronous**. You register a booking once, and the provider polls
the carrier for you. The first lookup of a *new* booking may therefore not have data yet. Bookings already
registered (in earlier runs) answer immediately. They are paid services.

## B.2 Provider comparison (researched 2026-11-05)

| Provider | Booking-number tracking | Model | Pricing | API | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ShipsGo (API v2)** | Yes: `booking_number` (or container) + carrier SCAC. MSC `MSCU`, Maersk `MAEU`, CMA `CMDU` listed as examples. Grimaldi: marketing pages exist; **confirm via `GET /ocean/carriers`**. | Async. `POST /ocean/shipments` once, then `GET` details (status `NEW` → `INPROGRESS` → data). **Duplicates return 409 with the existing shipment and no charge.** Server-side filter by `booking_number`. | Prepaid credits, 1 credit per new shipment; GETs are free. API-usage fee per the help center: none under 100 shipments/yr, custom between 100 and 2,000, one-time USD 500 at 2,000+. | Public OpenAPI 3.1 (`api.shipsgo.com/docs/v2/specs/openapi.json`). Header `X-Shipsgo-User-Token`. 100 req/min per company. Creates are processed serially (429 if concurrent). | **Recommended default:** cheapest for a small forwarder, simplest dedupe, fully documented. |
| Terminal49 | Yes for MSC/Maersk/CMA (`request_type: booking_number`). **No Grimaldi integration.** | Async: tracking request `pending` → `created` (can be `awaiting_manifest` up to 7 days), then a shipment. Webhooks. | Free plan: 10 active containers, and reading data via the API needs a trial or paid plan. Paid plans are per container (amounts not published). | JSON:API, `Authorization: Token …`, 100 req/min. Excellent docs (`terminal49.com/docs/llms.txt`). | Good alternative backend (§B.9). |
| Vizion | Booking numbers in **beta** (enable via support) for CMA, Evergreen, Maersk, MSC, ONE. No Grimaldi. | Async, webhook-centric, container-level child references. | Enterprise, via sales. | `X-API-Key`. Uses DCSA event codes. | Heavier than needed. |
| SeaRates (DP World) | Was synchronous `GET tracking.searates.com/tracking?api_key&number&sealine&type=BK`. | Sync. | Per container. | searates.com now redirects to dpworld.com, and the API host did not respond from our environment (2026-11-05). | **Avoid** until its status is clear. |
| Portcast, project44 | Yes (enterprise). | Async platform. | Enterprise contracts. | Large platforms. | Overkill for this tool. |

Data licensing: these providers obtain the data from carriers under their own agreements. Use the API
only as their terms allow (internal operational use).

## B.3 Access & onboarding (ShipsGo)

1. Create a company account at shipsgo.com. Sign-up includes a few free credits (help center: 3).
2. Dashboard → **Integrations → API Tokens** → create a token. The user must have the **Full Access** or
   **Co-Worker** role (Co-Worker Plus cannot manage other users' shipments).
3. Buy credits. For the API-usage fee, contact sales@shipsgo.com (see the tiers in §B.2). The expected cost
   is about one credit per booking over its whole life, because shipments are reused across runs (§B.7.3).
4. Put the token in `.env` as `AGG_API_TOKEN`. Then set `ETA_PROVIDER_<CARRIER>=aggregator` for the
   carriers it should serve (Part D).
5. Run the probe (§B.11) before the first real run.

## B.4 Configuration

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AggregatorSettings:
    api_token: str                                 # AGG_API_TOKEN — required; empty ⇒ settings.aggregator is None
    state_file: Path                               # derived: <ETA_STATE_DIR>/aggregator_tracking.json (not an env var)
    provider: str = "shipsgo"                      # AGG_PROVIDER — only "shipsgo" is implemented (others → ConfigError, §B.9)
    base_url: str = "https://api.shipsgo.com/v2"   # AGG_BASE_URL
    max_concurrency: int = 2                       # AGG_MAX_CONCURRENCY (03 §10)
    rate_per_minute: int = 90                      # AGG_RATE_PER_MINUTE (ShipsGo allows 100/min per company; keep headroom)
    timeout_s: float = 30.0                        # AGG_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
    allow_create: bool = True                      # AGG_ALLOW_CREATE — false = never spend credits; only read already-tracked bookings
    max_creates_per_run: int = 100                 # AGG_MAX_CREATES_PER_RUN — credit safety valve
    first_lookup_wait_s: int = 45                  # AGG_FIRST_LOOKUP_WAIT_S — how long get_eta polls a FRESH shipment (0 = no wait)
    poll_interval_s: int = 15                      # AGG_POLL_INTERVAL_S
    fresh_minutes: int = 30                        # AGG_FRESH_MINUTES — shipments first seen less than this ago are "fresh"
    scac: Mapping[Carrier, str] = field(default_factory=lambda: {
        Carrier.MSC: "MSCU", Carrier.MAERSK: "MAEU", Carrier.CMA: "CMDU", Carrier.GRIMALDI: "GRIU"})
                                                   # AGG_SCAC_MSC / AGG_SCAC_MAERSK / AGG_SCAC_CMA / AGG_SCAC_GRIMALDI
```

| Env var | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AGG_API_TOKEN` | yes, to enable | — | ShipsGo API token (secret: redacted everywhere) |
| `AGG_PROVIDER` | no | `shipsgo` | Backend (§B.9) |
| `AGG_BASE_URL` | no | `https://api.shipsgo.com/v2` | |
| `AGG_MAX_CONCURRENCY` | no | `2` | Parallel HTTP calls |
| `AGG_RATE_PER_MINUTE` | no | `90` | `AsyncLimiter(n, 60)` |
| `AGG_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | no | `30` | |
| `AGG_ALLOW_CREATE` | no | `true` | |
| `AGG_MAX_CREATES_PER_RUN` | no | `100` | |
| `AGG_FIRST_LOOKUP_WAIT_S` | no | `45` | |
| `AGG_POLL_INTERVAL_S` | no | `15` | |
| `AGG_FRESH_MINUTES` | no | `30` | |
| `AGG_SCAC_MSC` / `_MAERSK` / `_CMA` / `_GRIMALDI` | no | `MSCU` / `MAEU` / `CMDU` / `GRIU` | Carrier codes sent to the provider (Grimaldi's code is UNVERIFIED for ShipsGo; check the probe) |

Validation:
- Integers must be ≥ 0, except `rate_per_minute` and `max_concurrency`, which must be ≥ 1.
- `AGG_PROVIDER` other than `shipsgo` → `ConfigError("AGG_PROVIDER=<x> is described in 09 §B.9 but not implemented")`.

## B.5 Endpoints (ShipsGo API v2) — VERIFIED from the published OpenAPI (`ShipsGo API 2.0`)

Base `https://api.shipsgo.com/v2`. Every request sends:
- `X-Shipsgo-User-Token: <AGG_API_TOKEN>`
- `Accept: application/json`

POSTs send JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`).

| Purpose | Request | Success | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Find an existing shipment | `GET /ocean/shipments?filters[booking_number]=eq:{booking}&filters[carrier]=eq:{scac}&take=25` | 200 `{"message":"SUCCESS","shipments":[OceanShipmentsListData…],"meta":{"more":bool,"total":int\|null}}` | Filter syntax `filters[field]=operator:value`. `booking_number` supports `eq`. Free. |
| Create (start tracking) | `POST /ocean/shipments` body `{"booking_number": "<booking>", "carrier": "<SCAC>"}` | 200 `{"message":"SUCCESS","shipment":{"id":…}}`, or **409** `{"message":"ALREADY_EXISTS","shipment":{"id":…}}` (existing; **no charge**) | 402 `NOT_ENOUGH_CREDITS`; 422 bad payload. Creates are processed one at a time per company: concurrent creates can get 429 `TOO_MANY_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS`, so **serialise them**. Pattern: `booking_number` `^[a-zA-Z0-9/-]+$`, `carrier` `^(SG_)?[A-Z0-9]{4}$`. Do **not** send `reference`: it participates in duplicate detection. |
| Details | `GET /ocean/shipments/{id}` | 200 `{"message":"SUCCESS","shipment":OceanShipment}` | 404 means the shipment was deleted (e.g. in the dashboard). Free. |
| Carriers (probe only) | `GET /ocean/carriers?filters[status]=eq:ACTIVE&take=100&skip={n}` | 200 `{"carriers":[{"scac","name","status"}],"meta":{"more":…}}` | Page until `meta.more` is false. `filters[name]=contains:GRIMALDI` finds Grimaldi. |

Status codes:
- `401`: invalid token;
- `403`: role not allowed;
- `404`, `409`, `402`, `422` as above;
- `429`: rate limit (100 req/min per company). Headers `X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset`;
- `5xx`.

`OceanShipment` fields used:
- `id`, `booking_number`, `carrier{scac,name}`, `status`, `discarded_at`;
- `route.port_of_discharge{location{code,name,timezone,country}, date_of_discharge,
  date_of_discharge_initial, date_of_discharge_predicted}`;
- `containers[]{number, status, movements[]{event, status, location{code,name,timezone}, vessel{imo,name}|null,
  voyage, timestamp}}`.

Field values:
- `status` ∈ {NEW, INPROGRESS, BOOKED, LOADED, SAILING, ARRIVED, DISCHARGED, UNTRACKED}.
- Movement `event` ∈ {EMSH, GTIN, LOAD, DEPA, ARRV, DISC, GTOT, EMRT}, `status` ∈ {EST, ACT}.
- Movement `timestamp` is "ISO 8601 with timezone". **Which offset (UTC or local) is UNVERIFIED**, so always
  convert to `location.timezone` (§A.3.3, idempotent).
- `date_of_discharge` is "the date when the shipment is expected to be discharged".
- `date_of_discharge_predicted` is ShipsGo's own ML estimate. It is **not used**: the program reports
  carrier data only.
- `container.number` can be `NOT_ASSIGNED`.

## B.6 Auth

A static API token in a header. There is **no** `TokenProvider` and no `tokens.json` entry, and
`jwt_exp`/the token store are not used. Token providers must never acquire their semaphore (03 §8); that
does not apply here, because there is none. A 401/403 raises `CarrierLookupError` immediately (§B.7.6).

## B.7 Module design

### B.7.1 Public surface

```python
class AggregatorBookingError(CarrierLookupError):
    """A per-booking aggregator condition (not tracked yet / still fetching / UNTRACKED / creation cap reached).
    The circuit breaker (10 §6) must NOT count it: it says nothing about the provider being down."""

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class AggregatorSnapshot:
    tracking_id: str
    status: str                       # provider status, upper-case
    ready: bool                       # provider has carrier data
    failure: str | None               # permanent per-booking failure (e.g. "UNTRACKED"), else None
    pod_unlocode: str | None
    events: tuple[DcsaEvent, ...]     # provider movements adapted to DCSA (§B.7.4)
    route_pod_arrival: DcsaArrival | None
    containers: tuple[str, ...]
    raw: Mapping[str, Any]            # body as received (redact before logging/probe output)

class AggregatorBackend(Protocol):
    name: str                         # "ShipsGo" (used in messages and EtaResult.source)
    key: str                          # "shipsgo" (state-file namespace)
    async def find_existing(self, scac: str, booking: str) -> str | None: ...
    async def create(self, scac: str, booking: str) -> str: ...          # returns tracking id; 409 counts as success
    async def fetch(self, tracking_id: str) -> AggregatorSnapshot | None: ...   # None ⇔ HTTP 404
    async def list_carriers(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]: ...
    async def aclose(self) -> None: ...

class ShipsGoBackend:  # implements AggregatorBackend (§B.7.4)
    def __init__(self, settings: AggregatorSettings, *, http: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None): ...

class TrackingState:   # <ETA_STATE_DIR>/aggregator_tracking.json (§B.7.3)
    def __init__(self, path: Path): ...
    def get(self, provider_key: str, scac: str, booking: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None: ...
    def put(self, provider_key: str, scac: str, booking: str, entry: dict[str, Any]) -> None: ...
    def forget(self, provider_key: str, scac: str, booking: str) -> None: ...

class AggregatorClient:
    def __init__(self, settings: AggregatorSettings, *, backend: AggregatorBackend | None = None,
                 state: TrackingState | None = None, clock: Clock | None = None,
                 sleep: Callable[[float], Awaitable[None]] = asyncio.sleep): ...   # sleep injectable for tests
    def view(self, carrier: Carrier) -> CarrierClient: ...                         # cached per carrier
    async def prepare(self, items: Sequence[tuple[Carrier, str]]) -> dict[str, int]: ...
    async def get_eta(self, carrier: Carrier, booking: str) -> EtaResult: ...
    async def probe(self, carrier: Carrier | None, booking: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]: ...
    async def aclose(self) -> None: ...

class AggregatorCarrierView:   # implements CarrierClient (03 §9) for one carrier
    carrier: Carrier
    async def get_eta(self, booking: str) -> EtaResult        # → client.get_eta(self.carrier, booking)
    async def probe(self, booking: str) -> dict[str, Any]     # → client.probe(self.carrier, booking)
    async def aclose(self) -> None                            # no-op: the router closes the AggregatorClient once

def build_client(settings: Settings, token_store: TokenStore) -> AggregatorClient | None:
    """None when settings.aggregator is None. token_store is unused (static token).
    Unlike the carrier modules this returns the multi-carrier client; the router asks it for views."""

AGG_POLICY: Mapping[Carrier, Policy] = {Carrier.MSC: "first", Carrier.MAERSK: "first",
                                        Carrier.CMA: "latest", Carrier.GRIMALDI: "latest"}   # parity with 06/07/08
```

### B.7.2 HTTP rules (ShipsGoBackend)

- Construct an own `httpx.AsyncClient` via `http.new_async_client(base_url=settings.base_url,
  timeout=settings.timeout_s, headers={"X-Shipsgo-User-Token": token})`, unless one is injected.
  `aclose()` closes only an owned client.
- Every call goes through `http.request(..., service="aggregator", limiter=AsyncLimiter(rate_per_minute, 60))`.
  It holds the client's `asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrency)` **only around the HTTP call**, never across
  sleeps.
- The list and detail GETs and the carriers GET use `expected=(200,)`, with 404 allowed on details.
- Create uses `expected=(200, 409)` and the default `idempotent=False`. A read timeout on create is **not**
  retried, which avoids a double charge. The next run's `find_existing` picks the shipment up.
- Error mapping inside the backend (`ServiceError.status`):

  | Status | Error |
  |---|---|
  | 401 | `CarrierLookupError("ShipsGo rejected the API token (HTTP 401) — check AGG_API_TOKEN")` |
  | 403 | `CarrierLookupError("ShipsGo refused the operation (HTTP 403) — the token's user role may not create or read shipments")` |
  | 402 | `CarrierLookupError("ShipsGo: not enough credits to start tracking a new booking (HTTP 402) — buy credits or set AGG_ALLOW_CREATE=false")` |
  | 422 | `CarrierLookupError(f"ShipsGo rejected booking {booking} for carrier {scac} (HTTP 422): {message}")` |

  The 402 is systemic, so it stays a plain `CarrierLookupError` that the breaker counts.

### B.7.3 Tracking state (`aggregator_tracking.json`)

```json
{"version": 1,
 "entries": {"shipsgo:MSCU:EBKG12345678": {"tracking_id": "501234", "created_by_us": true,
             "first_seen_at": "2026-11-05T09:00:00", "last_status": "SAILING", "last_checked_at": "2026-11-05T09:01:10"}}}
```

- Key format: `f"{provider_key}:{scac}:{booking}"`. Times are naive local ISO from the injected clock.
- File handling:
  - load lazily;
  - a missing file is empty;
  - corrupt JSON → WARNING, treat as empty, and overwrite on the next `put`;
  - writes are atomic (temp file in the same directory + `os.replace`) under a `threading.Lock`.
- No secrets live in this file.
- Entries are never deleted automatically, except by `forget()` after a 404. A few hundred bytes per booking
  is fine.

### B.7.4 ShipsGo payload → snapshot

`fetch(id)`: GET details; 404 → `None`. Otherwise `sh = body["shipment"]`, and:
- `status = upper(sh["status"])`
- `ready`:
  - `status in {"BOOKED","LOADED","SAILING","ARRIVED","DISCHARGED"}` → True;
  - `{"NEW","INPROGRESS"}` → False;
  - `"UNTRACKED"` → False, with `failure="UNTRACKED"`;
  - any other value → `bool(sh.get("containers") or sh.get("route"))` (forward compatibility).
- `pod_unlocode = upper(route.port_of_discharge.location.code)`, if present.
- `route_pod_arrival`: if `route.port_of_discharge.date_of_discharge` is set →
  `DcsaArrival(eta=to_local_naive(date, pod_location.timezone), classifier="ACT" if status == "DISCHARGED" else "EST",
  unlocode=pod, facility_code=None, equipment_reference=None, basis="ROUTE POD date_of_discharge")`.
- `containers = tuple(upper(c.number) for c in containers if number and number != "NOT_ASSIGNED")`
- `events` = every movement of every container adapted to a `DcsaEvent`, as follows. Movements with an
  unknown `event`, a `status` other than EST/ACT, or an unparsable timestamp are skipped (DEBUG).

| ShipsGo `event` | `event_type` | `type_code` | `empty_indicator` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `EMSH` (empty to shipper) | EQUIPMENT | `GTOT` | `EMPTY` |
| `GTIN` | EQUIPMENT | `GTIN` | `LADEN` |
| `LOAD` | EQUIPMENT | `LOAD` | `LADEN` |
| `DEPA` | TRANSPORT | `DEPA` | — |
| `ARRV` | TRANSPORT | `ARRI` | — |
| `DISC` | EQUIPMENT | `DISC` | `LADEN` |
| `GTOT` | EQUIPMENT | `GTOT` | `LADEN` |
| `EMRT` (empty return) | EQUIPMENT | `GTIN` | `EMPTY` |

The other `DcsaEvent` fields:
- `classifier` = movement `status`;
- `event_datetime = to_local_naive(timestamp, location.timezone)`;
- `created_datetime = None`;
- `unlocode = upper(location.code)`;
- `mode_of_transport = "VESSEL"` if `vessel` is set, else `None`;
- `vessel_name = vessel.name`, `vessel_imo = str(vessel.imo)` (when not null);
- `voyage = movement.voyage`;
- `equipment_reference` = the container number (EQUIPMENT events only);
- `eq_refs = (number,)` for TRANSPORT events (ShipsGo movements are per container);
- `index` = running position;
- `raw` = the movement dict.

### B.7.5 `get_eta(carrier, booking)` — step by step

```
scac, policy = settings.scac[carrier], AGG_POLICY[carrier]
try:
    1. entry, tid, created_now = await self._ensure_tracking(carrier, scac, booking, allow_create=settings.allow_create)
    2. snap = await backend.fetch(tid)
       if snap is None:                                         # deleted provider-side → forget and re-resolve ONCE
           state.forget(...); entry, tid, created_now = await self._ensure_tracking(...); snap = await backend.fetch(tid)
           if snap is None: raise CarrierLookupError(f"ShipsGo lost shipment {tid} for booking {booking}")
    3. fresh = created_now or (clock.now() - parse(entry["first_seen_at"])) < timedelta(minutes=settings.fresh_minutes)
       deadline = monotonic() + settings.first_lookup_wait_s
       while fresh and not snap.ready and snap.failure is None and monotonic() < deadline:
           await self._sleep(settings.poll_interval_s)          # NOT holding the semaphore
           snap = await backend.fetch(tid) or snap
    4. state.put(..., {**entry, "last_status": snap.status, "last_checked_at": clock.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")})
    5. if snap.failure: raise AggregatorBookingError(
           f"ShipsGo could not track {carrier} booking {booking} (status {snap.failure}) — the number may be wrong "
           f"or {carrier} publishes no data for it")
       if not snap.ready: raise AggregatorBookingError(
           f"ShipsGo has not fetched {carrier} data for booking {booking} yet (status {snap.status}, "
           f"tracking since {entry['first_seen_at']}) — re-run later")
    6. arrival = dcsa.booking_arrival(snap.events, policy=policy, pod_unlocode=snap.pod_unlocode) or snap.route_pod_arrival
       if arrival is None: raise NoEtaError(
           f"ShipsGo found {carrier} booking {booking} but has no arrival date for the port of discharge. Can't determine ETA.")
    7. result = dcsa.to_eta_result(arrival, carrier=carrier, booking=booking, containers=snap.containers, source_prefix="ShipsGo")
       return replace(result, details={**result.details, "provider": "shipsgo", "tracking_id": tid,
                                        "status": snap.status, "policy": policy, "pod": snap.pod_unlocode})
except (CarrierLookupError, NoEtaError): raise
except AuthError as e:                    raise CarrierLookupError(f"ShipsGo authentication failed: {e}") from e
except ServiceError as e:                 raise CarrierLookupError(f"ShipsGo API error for booking {booking}: {e}") from e
except httpx.HTTPError as e:              raise CarrierLookupError(f"ShipsGo network error: {e!r}") from e
except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as e: raise CarrierLookupError(f"ShipsGo returned an unexpected payload: {e}") from e
```

`_ensure_tracking(carrier, scac, booking, *, allow_create) -> (entry, tracking_id, created_now)`:
1. `entry = state.get(...)`. If it is present, return it with `created_now=False`.
2. `tid = await backend.find_existing(scac, booking)`.
   - Pick the exact match: upper-case `booking_number` and `carrier.scac`.
   - If there are several, take the highest `id`.
   - If found, `put` it with `created_by_us=False` and `first_seen_at=now`, and return it.
3. If `not allow_create`, raise
   `AggregatorBookingError(f"{carrier} booking {booking} is not tracked in ShipsGo and AGG_ALLOW_CREATE=false")`.
4. If `self._creates >= settings.max_creates_per_run`, raise
   `AggregatorBookingError(f"AGG_MAX_CREATES_PER_RUN ({n}) reached — booking {booking} not registered with ShipsGo this run")`.
5. Under the client's **create lock** (an `asyncio.Lock`, so creates are serial):
   - re-check the state, because another coroutine may have just created it;
   - `tid = await backend.create(scac, booking)`;
   - `self._creates += 1`, but only when the response was 200, not 409. The backend reports this through a
     `last_create_was_new` flag, or by returning `(tid, is_new)`; the implementer chooses.
   - `put(created_by_us=True, first_seen_at=now)`;
   - return with `created_now=True`.

`prepare(items)`:
- De-duplicate the items.
- For each `(carrier, booking)`, **sequentially**: call `_ensure_tracking(..., allow_create=settings.allow_create)`.
  Catch every exception and log it as a WARNING; `get_eta` re-raises properly later.
- Return counts `{"known","found","created","failed"}`, and log them at INFO.
- Called once per run by the router (Part D) **before** the per-row tasks start. New bookings then have the
  whole planning phase to become ready.

`probe(carrier, booking)` **never creates** (it costs a credit). It returns:
- `{"provider": "shipsgo", "account_ok": bool, "carriers": [ACTIVE carriers whose scac is in settings.scac values or whose name contains GRIMALDI]}`;
- with a booking:
  - `"state_entry"`, `"find_existing"` (id or None);
  - if tracked: `"raw"` (redacted body), `"snapshot": {status, ready, failure, pod, containers}`,
    `"explain": dcsa.explain_selection(...)`, and `"eta"` (`EtaResult` as a dict, or an error string);
  - otherwise `"note": "not tracked yet — eta run / eta eta would register it (1 credit)"`.

The token must never appear in the output.

### B.7.6 Deviations and notes

- **DEVIATION (MSC via aggregator):** MSC's customs-hold heuristic and its "Full Transshipment Loaded + 7
  days" fallback (06) are MSC-GraphQL rules. They are **not** applied when MSC is routed to the aggregator.
  A booking without a POD date raises `NoEtaError`.
- **Freshness:** ShipsGo refreshes on its own schedule (UNVERIFIED frequency). Dates can lag the carrier's
  site by hours, which is acceptable for a 6-business-day window.
- **First sight of a booking:**
  - it may fail with "re-run later" (`AggregatorBookingError` → `Failed_To_Process.txt`, Carrier Lookup
    Failed);
  - the next run, usually the next day, has data;
  - `AGG_FIRST_LOOKUP_WAIT_S` trades run time for fewer such rows.

## B.8 Fallbacks

- If the aggregator is not configured, rows routed to it fail with the configuration message (Part D).
- If ShipsGo is down, the circuit breaker (10 §6) stops hammering it after N consecutive non-booking
  failures.
- Staff can switch a carrier back with `ETA_PROVIDER_<X>=native` once official access is approved.

## B.9 Swapping providers (Terminal49 outline)

Implement another `AggregatorBackend`; nothing else changes. For Terminal49:
- **Requests:**
  - base `https://api.terminal49.com/v2`;
  - headers `Authorization: Token <key>` and `Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json`;
  - limits: 100 req/min; 100 creates/min.
- **`find_existing`:** `GET /tracking_requests?filter[request_number]={booking}&filter[scac]={scac}&include=tracked_object`
  → the newest `data[]` item with `request_type == "booking_number"`.
- **`create`:** `POST /tracking_requests` with
  `{"data":{"type":"tracking_request","attributes":{"request_type":"booking_number","request_number":booking,"scac":scac}}}`
  → 201 `data.id` (status `pending`). A 422 means a bad or unsupported SCAC.
- **`fetch`:** `GET /tracking_requests/{id}`. By `status`:

  | `status` | Snapshot |
  |---|---|
  | `pending` / `awaiting_manifest` | not ready |
  | `failed` / `cancelled` | `failure = failed_reason` (e.g. `not_found`, `duplicate`, `data_unavailable`, `booking_cancelled`) |
  | `created` / `tracking_stopped` | ready; continue below |

  When ready, read `relationships.tracked_object.data.id`, then
  `GET /shipments/{sid}?include=containers`. Events:
  - each container's `attributes.pod_discharged_at` → EQUIPMENT DISC ACT;
  - `attributes.pod_arrived_at` → TRANSPORT ARRI ACT with `eq_refs=(number,)`;
  - shipment `pod_ata_at` → TRANSPORT ARRI ACT;
  - else `pod_eta_at` → TRANSPORT ARRI EST.

  Time zone: `pod_timezone`. `pod_unlocode`: `port_of_discharge_locode`.
- **Cost and coverage:** the free plan covers 10 active containers, and reading data needs a trial or paid
  plan. There is no Grimaldi coverage.

Expected results (computed with the reference implementation):

| Case | Expected |
|---|---|
| Sailing, `view(MSC)` (policy `first`) | `eta == datetime(2026,11,12,7,30)` (12:30Z → New York, EST); `is_actual False`; `source == "ShipsGo TRANSPORT ARRI EST at USNYC"`; `containers == ("MEDU1234567","MEDU7654321")`; `details["tracking_id"] == "501234"` |
| Sailing payload via `view(CMA)` (policy `latest`) | `eta == datetime(2026,11,14,6,0)` (box 2) |
| Discharged | `eta == datetime(2026,11,2,21,40)`; `is_actual True`; `source == "ShipsGo EQUIPMENT DISC ACT at USNYC"` |
| Sailing with `containers` emptied | Route fallback: `eta == datetime(2026,11,12,13,0)` (18:00Z → local), EST, basis `ROUTE POD date_of_discharge` |
| In progress, `AGG_FIRST_LOOKUP_WAIT_S=0` | `AggregatorBookingError`, message contains "re-run later" |
| Untracked | `AggregatorBookingError`, message contains "could not track" |

Tests (respx router on `https://api.shipsgo.test/v2`; `sleep` injected as an async no-op; `FixedClock`):
1. `test_build_client_none_when_unconfigured`.
2. `test_known_state_entry_skips_lookup`: one detail GET, no list, no create.
3. `test_existing_found_by_list_no_create`: the list returns the shipment → no POST; the state is written
   with `created_by_us False`.
4. `test_create_when_absent`: empty list → POST body exactly `{"booking_number": "EBKG87654321", "carrier": "MSCU"}`
   with the token header → state `created_by_us True` → detail fetched.
5. `test_create_409_is_success_and_not_counted`.
6. `test_create_402_plain_lookup_error`: a `CarrierLookupError` that is **not** an `AggregatorBookingError`;
   the message mentions credits.
7. `test_allow_create_false`: not found → `AggregatorBookingError`, zero POSTs.
8. `test_create_cap`: with `AGG_MAX_CREATES_PER_RUN=1`, the second new booking → `AggregatorBookingError`;
   an already-tracked booking still succeeds.
9. `test_creates_are_serialised`: 3 concurrent new bookings. A respx side effect asserts that no two POSTs
   overlap (it counts in-flight requests).
10. `test_inprogress_then_ready`: details return in-progress, then sailing, with wait 30 and interval 10 →
    success after 2 GETs.
11. `test_inprogress_no_wait`: wait 0 → "re-run later".
12. `test_stale_entry_not_waited`: `first_seen_at` 2 days ago and status `INPROGRESS` → immediate error, one
    GET.
13. `test_untracked`.
14. `test_detail_404_forgets_and_retries_once`.
15. `test_expected_results[...]`: the table above, including the CMA policy and the route fallback.
16. `test_401_message_mentions_token_var`.
17. `test_probe_never_creates_and_redacts`: zero POSTs; `json.dumps(output)` does not contain the token;
    the explain lines are present.
18. `test_state_file_corrupt_is_tolerated` and `test_state_file_atomic_write` (no partial file after a
    simulated exception).
19. `test_prepare_counts_and_sequential`: mixed known, found and created items give the right counts, and
    exceptions are swallowed.
20. `test_view_aclose_noop`: closing a view does not close the shared client.

## B.11 Probe / verification (safe, real account)

1. `eta probe aggregator`: shows `account_ok` and the ACTIVE carriers. Confirm `MSCU`, `MAEU` and `CMDU`,
   and find Grimaldi's code. If it is not `GRIU`, set `AGG_SCAC_GRIMALDI`.
2. `eta probe aggregator --booking <a booking you already track in the ShipsGo dashboard>`. The carrier is
   derived from the booking pattern. Check the explained POD/ETA against the ShipsGo dashboard and the
   carrier's site. This verifies the time zone conversion.
3. `eta eta <one new booking>`. This registers it (1 credit) and may say "re-run later". Run it again after a
   few minutes; it should now return an ETA.
4. Only then set `ETA_PROVIDER_<X>=aggregator` for real runs.

---

# Part C — Grimaldi (`carriers/grimaldi.py`)

## C.1 Verdict

- **No public tracking API was found.**
  - Grimaldi (booking pattern `S3` + 8 digits) is **not** a DCSA member. The members are Maersk, MSC,
    CMA CGM, Hapag-Lloyd, ONE, Evergreen, HMM, Yang Ming and ZIM (plus later joiners such as PIL).
  - No DCSA or proprietary API documentation exists publicly.
  - Public tracking is the GNET eService web portal (`gnet.grimaldi-eservice.com`). Automating it would mean
    browser automation or scraping, which this program rules out.
- **Aggregators:**
  - Terminal49 states it "does not yet integrate Grimaldi Lines's feed".
  - Vizion's booking beta does not list it.
  - ShipsGo, GoComet, project44 and Visiwise advertise Grimaldi container tracking, but **booking-number**
    support via API is UNVERIFIED.
- **SCAC:** `GRIU` according to SeaRates, Beacon and Safecube. It is UNVERIFIED for ShipsGo.

So the default stays **parity**: Grimaldi rows fail with the original message. If the ShipsGo probe shows
Grimaldi as ACTIVE, set `ETA_PROVIDER_GRIMALDI=aggregator`, and confirm one booking with §B.11 steps 2–3
before relying on it. You can also ask Grimaldi's eService team whether they offer EDI (IFTSTA) or an API to
customers.

## C.2 Module design

```python
GRIMALDI_NOT_IMPLEMENTED = "Grimaldi ETA lookup not yet implemented for booking {booking}"   # exact original text

class GrimaldiClient:                    # implements CarrierClient
    carrier = Carrier.GRIMALDI
    async def get_eta(self, booking: str) -> EtaResult:
        raise UnsupportedCarrierError(GRIMALDI_NOT_IMPLEMENTED.format(booking=booking))
    async def probe(self, booking: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {"requests": [], "raw": None, "eta": GRIMALDI_NOT_IMPLEMENTED.format(booking=booking),
                "note": "No Grimaldi API; see 09 Part C. Use ETA_PROVIDER_GRIMALDI=aggregator if your aggregator covers it."}
    async def aclose(self) -> None: return None

def build_client(settings: Settings, token_store: TokenStore) -> GrimaldiClient:
    return GrimaldiClient()              # always "configured" — it needs nothing
```

## C.3 Tests (`tests/test_grimaldi.py`)

1. `get_eta("S312345678")` raises `UnsupportedCarrierError` whose `str` is exactly
   `Grimaldi ETA lookup not yet implemented for booking S312345678`.
2. `probe()` returns the same text and makes no HTTP call.

# Part D — Provider selection (`carriers/router.py`)

01 §4 owns the booking-number patterns and their messages. This part owns what happens **after** a carrier
is identified.

## D.1 Configuration

`RunSettings.providers: Mapping[Carrier, Literal["native", "aggregator", "off"]]` (02 §1), read from:

| Env var | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `ETA_PROVIDER_MSC` | `native` | `native` \| `aggregator` \| `off` (case-insensitive, stripped) |
| `ETA_PROVIDER_MAERSK` | `native` | same |
| `ETA_PROVIDER_CMA` | `native` | same |
| `ETA_PROVIDER_GRIMALDI` | `off` | same (`native` and `off` both mean the parity stub) |

Any other value raises `ConfigError(f"ETA_PROVIDER_{X} must be one of native, aggregator, off (got {value!r})")`
in `load_settings()`.

## D.2 `CarrierRouter`

```python
class CarrierRouter:
    def __init__(self, *, providers: Mapping[Carrier, str],
                 native: Mapping[Carrier, CarrierClient | None],      # from each carrier module's build_client()
                 native_missing: Mapping[Carrier, tuple[str, ...]],   # env var names for the "not configured" message (Settings.missing)
                 aggregator: AggregatorClient | None,
                 failure_limit: int): ...
    def route(self, base: str) -> tuple[Carrier, str, CarrierClient]: ...
    async def prepare(self, bases: Sequence[str]) -> None: ...
    async def aclose(self) -> None: ...
```

`route(base)`:
1. Apply the 01 §4 pattern table to get `(carrier, token)`. This includes its `UnsupportedCarrierError`s
   (reference number, no pattern) and the D6 extra-text `CarrierLookupError`.
2. `provider = providers[carrier]`; the message suffix `X = carrier.name` (`MSC`, `MAERSK`, `CMA`, `GRIMALDI`).
3. `carrier is Carrier.GRIMALDI and provider in ("native", "off")` →
   `raise UnsupportedCarrierError(GRIMALDI_NOT_IMPLEMENTED.format(booking=token))`. This is the exact original
   text, and parity is why Grimaldi's `off` does not use the generic message.
4. `provider == "off"` → `raise CarrierLookupError(f"{carrier} lookups are disabled (ETA_PROVIDER_{X}=off)")`.
5. `provider == "aggregator"`:
   - if `aggregator is None`, raise
     `CarrierLookupError(f"{carrier} is set to use the aggregator (ETA_PROVIDER_{X}=aggregator) but the aggregator is not configured — set AGG_API_TOKEN in .env")`;
   - otherwise return `(carrier, token, self._breaker(aggregator.view(carrier)))`.
6. `native` → `client = native[carrier]`:
   - if it is `None`, raise
     `CarrierLookupError(f"{carrier} lookups are not configured — set {', '.join(native_missing[carrier])} in .env")`
     (03 §9);
   - otherwise return `(carrier, token, self._breaker(client))`.

Route-time errors are raised **before** any client is called, so the circuit breaker never sees them.

Circuit breaker (10 §6) additions:
- Keep one breaker per `(provider, carrier)`.
- **Do not count** `UnsupportedCarrierError`, `AggregatorBookingError`, `NoEtaError` or `CustomsHoldError`.
- Count only other `CarrierLookupError`s.

`prepare(bases)`:
- For each base booking, try `route()`. Ignore errors; the per-row task reports them later.
- Collect `(carrier, token)` pairs that resolved to the aggregator.
- If there are any, `await aggregator.prepare(pairs)`.
- No-op without an aggregator.
- **Pipeline hook (10 Phase 2):** call it once, before the per-row tasks start, with the base booking of
  every row that will need an ETA. Those are the STANDARD and NOTIF1_SENT rows at or above the amount
  threshold.

`aclose()`: close every native client once, and the aggregator once. Views are no-ops.

## D.3 Tests (`tests/test_router.py`, in addition to 12-testing's pattern tests)

1. `off` → the exact disabled message; no client is called.
2. `aggregator` with no aggregator → the message names `AGG_API_TOKEN`.
3. `aggregator` → the returned client is a view with the right `carrier`. `get_eta` forwards the carrier.
4. Grimaldi:
   - default (`off`) → `UnsupportedCarrierError` with the exact original text;
   - `native` → same;
   - `aggregator` → a view.
5. Native not configured → the message lists the missing env vars.
6. An invalid `ETA_PROVIDER_CMA=shipsgo` → `ConfigError` at load.
7. `prepare()` forwards only aggregator-routed pairs, de-duplicated, and survives route errors.
8. Breaker: 6 consecutive `AggregatorBookingError`s do not trip it; 5 consecutive plain
   `CarrierLookupError`s from the aggregator view do.

# 10 — Pipeline: plan → confirm → apply (`pipeline.py`, `outputs.py`, `ledger.py`)

## 1. Why the new pipeline is fast

The original `mainIG.main()` processed one row at a time, and for each row it might: launch a browser for
the carrier (MSC headless; Maersk and CMA headful Chrome with multi-second warm-ups), drive the QuickBooks
SPA with `slow_mo=200` ms per action plus fixed sleeps, and search VShip several times. That is roughly
30–90 s per row, i.e. hours for a ~500-row file.

The new pipeline:
1. does **all reads first, concurrently** (carrier ETAs, VShip lookups, one batched QBO query),
2. shows a **plan** and asks for confirmation (or `--dry-run` stops here),
3. performs the **writes concurrently across rows** (sequentially within a row), each a single API call.

Expected wall time for ~400 actionable rows: a few minutes end-to-end, dominated by carrier API latency and
by e-mail sending (see 04-quickbooks-online.md for whether sends must be serialized). These are estimates —
the run report records real per-phase timings.

## 2. Models (`models.py`, in addition to 03-foundations §4)

```python
class RowKind(StrEnum):
    MALFORMED = "MALFORMED"; STANDARD = "STANDARD"; NOTIF1_SENT = "NOTIF1_SENT"
    BOTH_SENT = "BOTH_SENT"; SKIP_R = "SKIP_R"; MANUAL = "MANUAL"

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class InputRow:
    line_no: int
    doc_number: str
    amount_raw: str
    amount: Decimal | None
    parse_error: str | None           # e.g. "could not convert string to float: 'abc'"

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ParsedRow:
    row: InputRow
    kind: RowKind
    base_booking: str | None          # stripped + upper-cased (01 §3)

class Route(StrEnum):
    FAILED = "FAILED"; CUSTOMS_HOLD = "CUSTOMS_HOLD"; SKIPPED = "SKIPPED"
    BINDU = "BINDU"; BEN = "BEN"; ACCOUNTING = "ACCOUNTING"
    PAID_UPDATE = "PAID_UPDATE"; NOTIFY = "NOTIFY"; FUTURE_UPDATE = "FUTURE_UPDATE"

class OutputFile(StrEnum):
    BINDU = "Send2Bindu.csv"; BEN = "Send2Ben.txt"; ACCOUNTING = "Send2Accounting.txt"
    FAILED = "Failed_To_Process.txt"; CUSTOMS = "PotentialCustomsHold.txt"

# Side-effect actions, executed in list order during apply
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class QboUpdate:      eta: date; new_doc_number: str | None = None
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class QboSend:        subject: str
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class VShipComment:   text: str
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class VShipPatchEta:  eta: datetime
Action = QboUpdate | QboSend | VShipComment | VShipPatchEta

@dataclass
class Plan:
    parsed: ParsedRow
    route: Route
    message: str = ""                     # Failed/routed entry text (01 §14) or human reason
    output: tuple[OutputFile, str | list[str]] | None = None   # entry to write for routed/failed rows
    carrier: Carrier | None = None
    eta: EtaResult | None = None
    cutoff: datetime | None = None
    in_window: bool | None = None
    notif: NotifStatus | None = None
    notif_defaulted: bool = False         # 01 §6.2 'send' default applied
    invoice: InvoiceSnapshot | None = None
    vship_booking_id: str | None = None
    vship_error: str | None = None        # VShip id/comments could not be read in the plan phase
    actions: list[Action] = field(default_factory=list)
    warnings: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    # filled during apply
    status: Literal["PENDING", "OK", "FAILED", "ROUTED", "SKIPPED", "INTERRUPTED"] = "PENDING"
    done: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    error: str | None = None
```

## 3. Services container

```python
@dataclass
class Services:
    settings: Settings
    clock: Clock                          # FixedClock(run_now) — every client gets the same instant
    token_store: TokenStore
    qbo: QboClient
    vship: VShipClient
    router: CarrierRouter                 # carriers/router.py: route(base) -> (Carrier, token, CarrierClient)
    outputs: OutputWriter
    ledger: Ledger

@asynccontextmanager
async def build_services(settings: Settings, run_now: datetime, *, read_only: bool) -> AsyncIterator[Services]:
    """Creates TokenStore(<ETA_STATE_DIR>/tokens.json), the QBO client via build_qbo(settings, token_store,
    read_only=read_only) (04 §6.8), VShipAuth/VShipClient(read_only=read_only), every carrier client via its
    build_client(), the router, OutputWriter(enabled=not read_only), Ledger.
    On exit: aclose() every client (in a finally) — QboClient.aclose() also closes the e-mail strategy, which
    restores the QBO template if a recovery record exists (04b §6.2)."""
```

## 4. Phases

```python
async def run(settings: Settings, input_csv: Path, *, dry_run: bool, assume_yes: bool, force: bool,
              no_email: bool, only: set[str] | None, limit: int | None,
              clock: Clock = SystemClock()) -> RunSummary:
    # RunSummary: counts per Route and status, phase timings, report/log paths, email_blocked, exit_code
```

### Phase 0 — preflight (sequential, fail fast)
1. `run_now = clock.now()`; `run_id = run_now.strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")`.
2. Create `ETA_OUTPUT_DIR`, `ETA_OUTPUT_DIR/reports`, `ETA_OUTPUT_DIR/logs`, `ETA_STATE_DIR` if missing.
3. Unless `dry_run`: enter `run_lock(state_dir)` (03 §14) for the rest of the run; `RunLockedError` → exit code 2.
4. `require(settings, "qbo", "vship")` (03 §12) → `ConfigError` lists every missing variable → exit code 2.
5. `async with build_services(settings, run_now, read_only=dry_run)`: the QBO client is built with
   `read_only=dry_run` (04 §6.1) and the VShip client likewise (05 §6.2), so a dry run cannot write even by mistake.
6. Authenticate QBO (`await qbo_auth.get_token()`) and VShip (`await vship_auth.get_token()`). Failure →
   print a clear message (which variable / which command to run, e.g. `eta qbo-auth`) and exit code 2.
   Carrier auth is lazy (first lookup), guarded by the circuit breaker (§6).
   (The e-mail strategy's crash recovery and verification gate run in Phase 3 — see step 2 there.)

### Phase 1 — read & classify (pure)
`rows = read_input(input_csv)` → `parsed = [classify(r) for r in rows]` (01 §2–3), then apply D2 (header),
D3 (duplicates), `--only` (keep rows whose `doc_number` or `base_booking` is in the set) and `--limit N`
(first N remaining rows). Log `Loaded {n} booking(s) from file.`; if zero → print
`Invoice list is empty - nothing to do.` and exit 0.

**MSC token pre-flight** (06 §5.1, only when MSC runs in `mymsc` bridge mode and at least one row routes to
MSC): read `token_status()`; if there is no token or `seconds_left < 600`, prompt for one on a TTY
(`getpass`, same as `eta msc-token`); without a TTY, fail fast with the 06 §5.1 message (exit code 2) — before
any lookup or write. In `api` mode nothing is needed.

### Phase 2 — plan (read-only, concurrent)
First, once: `await router.prepare(bases)` with the base booking of every STANDARD / NOTIF1_SENT row at or
above the amount threshold (09 §D.2 — lets the optional aggregator register new bookings in one serialized
batch; a no-op without an aggregator).

Then all rows run as tasks in an `asyncio.TaskGroup`, bounded by `asyncio.Semaphore(ETA_MAX_PARALLEL_BOOKINGS)`.
A task never raises: every exception is converted into a `Plan` with route FAILED and the right 01 §14 entry.

**2a — per-row lookups**
```
MALFORMED  → Plan(FAILED, output=(FAILED, malformed entry))
SKIP_R     → Plan(SKIPPED)
MANUAL     → Plan(FAILED, output=(FAILED, doc_number))
amount < threshold (STANDARD/NOTIF1_SENT/BOTH_SENT)
           → name = await vship.get_customer_name(base) (errors → "" + warning, D14)
             Plan(BINDU, output=(BINDU, [doc, amount_raw, name]))
BOTH_SENT  → Plan(BEN, output=(BEN, doc))
STANDARD / NOTIF1_SENT:
   carrier, token, client = router.route(base)            # UnsupportedCarrierError → 01 §6.1
   eta = await client.get_eta(token)                      # errors → 01 §6.1 (CUSTOMS_HOLD route for CustomsHoldError)
   cutoff = window_cutoff(run_now, ETA_WINDOW_BUSINESS_DAYS); in_window = eta.eta <= cutoff
   try:  booking_id = await vship.find_booking_id(base)
   except Exception as e: vship_error = str(e)
   if in_window:
       try:  comments = await vship.get_internal_comments(booking_id)   (skipped if vship_error)
             notif = notif_status(comments, run_now)
       except/if vship_error: apply ETA_ON_NOTIF_LOOKUP_ERROR (01 §6.2) → notif = NotifStatus(0, True), notif_defaulted=True
                              or Plan(FAILED, "VShip notification lookup failed, nothing sent")
       notif.count == 2   → Plan(BEN, output=(BEN, doc))
       not have_to_do     → Plan(FAILED, output=(FAILED, "[SKIP] #{doc} - Done in the last week"))
       else               → mark "needs QBO" (in-window)
   else                   → mark "needs QBO" (out-of-window)
```

**2b — one batched QBO lookup**
`invoices = await qbo.find_invoices_by_doc_numbers(sorted({p.parsed.row.doc_number for p in needs_qbo}))`.
A QBO lookup failure here (network/auth) fails every pending row with
`[ERROR] #{doc} - QB Invoice Processing Error, No Email Sent\n{err}\n`.
A DocNumber listed in `qbo.ambiguous` (several invoices share it — 04 §6.3) fails with the same template and
the `AmbiguousInvoiceError` text (**D21**: the original silently used the first match).

**2c — finalize decisions (pure except the TR/SWB comments fetch, which is already cached)**
```
inv missing                     → FAILED "[SKIP] #{doc} - not found in QuickBooks"
in-window and inv.is_paid       → PAID_UPDATE  actions=[QboUpdate(eta.date()), VShipPatchEta(eta)]
in-window, partially paid:
    vship_error                 → FAILED "QB Invoice Processing Error, No Email Sent" + vship_error   (01 §6.7)
    has_tr_swb_note(comments)   → ACCOUNTING output=(ACCOUNTING, f"{doc} - is partially paid and has a TR/SWB note")
    else                        → NOTIFY (below)
in-window otherwise             → NOTIFY
out-of-window                   → FUTURE_UPDATE actions=[QboUpdate(eta.date()),
                                                       VShipComment(vship_comment_for(eta, notif_index=0, now=run_now)),
                                                       VShipPatchEta(eta)]
NOTIFY:
    subject = subject_for(inv.doc_number, eta, notif_sent=(notif.count == 1), paid=False, now=run_now)
    new_doc = with_arrival_suffix(inv.doc_number) if eta.date() <= today else None
    actions = [QboUpdate(eta.date(), new_doc), QboSend(subject),
               VShipComment(vship_comment_for(eta, notif_index=(1 if notif.count == 1 else 0), now=run_now)),
               VShipPatchEta(eta)]
    guards (each → FAILED "QB Invoice Processing Error, No Email Sent\n<reason>"):
        - inv.recipients is empty  → reason "Invoice has no customer e-mail address (BillEmail)"
        - new_doc and (reason := doc_number_problem(new_doc, settings.qbo)) → that reason (04 §7)
    ledger guard (unless --force): ledger.emailed_on(inv.id, today) → FAILED
        "[SKIP] #{doc} - already e-mailed today at {HH:MM} (ledger); use --force to resend"
```
Where `eta` above means `plan.eta.eta` (the datetime) and `doc` the input doc_number.

### Phase 3 — review & confirm
1. **`--no-email` transformation** (11-cli): every NOTIFY plan keeps only
   `[QboUpdate(eta.date(), new_doc_number=None), VShipPatchEta(eta)]` — no e-mail, no DocNumber suffix and no
   VShip note (the suffix and the `NOTIF #n`/`ARRIVING` note are the records that a notice was sent, so they are
   left for whoever sends the e-mail by hand). Its would-be subject, recipients, suffixed DocNumber and note
   text are written to `<ETA_OUTPUT_DIR>/ToEmail_<run_id>.csv`
   (`doc_number, invoice_id, customer, to, cc, subject, doc_number_after_sending, vship_note_after_sending`)
   during Phase 4. Such rows end as OK with message `e-mail pending (manual send, --no-email)`.
2. **E-mail path preflight** — only if at least one plan still contains a `QboSend`:
   `await qbo.prepare_for_sending(dry_run=dry_run)` (04 §6.6, 04b §6.2/§6.3). In a real run this also
   restores a QBO e-mail template left modified by a crashed run (04b crash recovery) — a repair, so it is
   done before the prompt. If it raises `EmailPathUnavailableError` (including `TemplateRestoreError`):
   print the message prominently, convert every NOTIFY plan to FAILED with
   `[ERROR] #{doc} - QB Invoice Processing Error, No Email Sent\n{err}\n`, set `email_blocked = True`
   (exit code 4 at the end), and continue — the other routes can still be applied.
3. Write the plan report (§7) — always, also in dry-run.
4. Print the summary (§8): counts per route, then every NOTIFY row
   (`doc → new doc | subject | to: recipients`), every PAID_UPDATE/FUTURE_UPDATE row (`doc → ETA`), and all
   warnings (e.g. `notif lookup failed — defaulting to send`, `MSC other containers disagree`).
5. `--dry-run` → stop here; print `Dry run: nothing was changed. Plan saved to <path>`; exit 0.
6. If there are no actions → skip to Phase 5.
7. Unless `--yes`: prompt `Apply {n_actions} change(s) to {n_rows} invoice(s) and send {n_emails} e-mail(s)? [y/N] `
   (read it with `await asyncio.to_thread(input, prompt)` so the event loop is not blocked).
   If stdin is not a TTY and `--yes` was not given → abort with a message (exit code 3). Anything but `y`/`yes` → abort.

### Phase 4 — apply (writes)
1. Write every routed/failed entry produced in Phase 2 to its output file **in input order** (§5).
   Mark those plans ROUTED / FAILED / SKIPPED.
2. Run every plan with actions as a task (TaskGroup + `ETA_MAX_PARALLEL_BOOKINGS` semaphore). Within a plan,
   execute actions in order:
   - `QboUpdate` → `inv = await qbo.update_invoice(inv, eta=a.eta, doc_number=a.new_doc_number)`; ledger record.
   - `QboSend` → `receipt = await qbo.send_invoice(inv, subject=a.subject)`; ledger record (`emailed`, with the
     receipt's strategy, recipients and `sent_at`/`qbo_delivery_time`; never the body).
     On failure, if a previous `QboUpdate` changed the DocNumber, attempt the D11 revert
     (`update_invoice(updated, doc_number=original)`) and append
     `"(invoice number reverted to <old>)"` or `"(could not revert invoice number: <err>)"` to the error.
     If the failure is `EmailPathUnavailableError`/`TemplateRestoreError`: set `email_blocked = True`, and every
     NOTIFY plan that has **not started yet** is failed (without running any of its actions) with
     `[ERROR] #{doc} - QB Invoice Processing Error, No Email Sent\n{err}\n`; non-NOTIFY plans keep running.
     Exception order matters: check `TemplateRestoreError`/`EmailPathUnavailableError` before plain `InvoiceSendError`.
   - NOTIFY plans start their `QboUpdate` only after Phase 3's e-mail preflight succeeded, so a blocked e-mail
     path can never leave a suffixed DocNumber without an e-mail.
   - `VShipComment` → `await vship.post_comment(booking_id, a.text)` (if `vship_booking_id` is None, raise the
     stored `vship_error` as `NoteError`); ledger record.
   - `VShipPatchEta` → `await vship.patch_expected_arrival(booking_id, a.eta)`; ledger record.
   - Map the first failure to 01 §6.6, append it to Failed_To_Process.txt immediately, mark FAILED, stop the plan.
   - All done → log `[OK]    #{doc}`, mark OK.
3. Ctrl+C / cancellation: stop starting new plans; plans already running finish their *current* action, then
   stop; remaining plans are INTERRUPTED (listed in the report). Cleanup (e-mail strategy restore, client close)
   always runs.

### Phase 5 — report
Print `Done: {ok} succeeded, {failed} failed/skipped.` (01 §13), the per-route table, phase timings, and paths
of the report/log files. Rewrite the run report with final statuses. Exit code 0, or **4** if `email_blocked`
(the e-mail path failed; print the 04b manual-restore instructions again if a `TemplateRestoreError` occurred).

## 5. `outputs.py`

```python
class OutputWriter:
    def __init__(self, output_dir: Path, *, enabled: bool): ...   # enabled=False in dry-run
    def write(self, file: OutputFile, entry: str | list[str]) -> None:
        """Append one entry. Text files: f.write(entry + "\\n") (entry may contain newlines).
        Send2Bindu.csv: csv.writer(f).writerow(entry) with newline=""; if the file is new, write a UTF-8 BOM first.
        Opens/closes the file per call (crash-safe), encoding utf-8, guarded by a threading.Lock."""
```

## 6. Carrier lookup memo and circuit breaker

**Memo (single-flight).** The router memoizes `get_eta` per `(carrier, query token)` for the whole run:
the first caller creates an `asyncio.Task`, later callers await the same task (`asyncio.shield`), and both
results and exceptions are memoized. Two input rows for the same booking (e.g. `NAM1234567` and
`NAM1234567 A`) therefore cost one carrier call — important because some carrier APIs bill per call
(08-carrier-cma-cgm.md §2). Carrier clients may also memoize internally (CMA does); the two layers are
compatible. `probe` bypasses the memo.

The router itself (provider selection `ETA_PROVIDER_<CARRIER>`, `route()`, `prepare()`) is specified in
09 Part D; the memo above and the breaker below are its additional responsibilities.

**Circuit breaker.** The router also tracks, per `(provider, carrier)`, the run of consecutive
`CarrierLookupError`s whose **message text is identical**. It never counts `UnsupportedCarrierError`,
`AggregatorBookingError`, `NoEtaError` or `CustomsHoldError` (09 §D.2), and route-time errors are raised before
any client is called, so they never reach it. Per-booking failures such as
"no record of booking NAM1234567" contain the booking number, so their texts differ and never trip the
breaker; service-level failures (rejected credentials, product not approved, network down) produce the
same text for every booking. After `ETA_CARRIER_FAILURE_LIMIT` (default 5) identical consecutive failures,
further rows for that carrier fail fast, without a network call, with
`CarrierLookupError(f"{carrier} lookups aborted after {n} identical consecutive failures; last error: {last}")`.
Any success or differently-worded failure resets the count. Memoized duplicates (above) are not counted twice.

## 7. Run report (`<ETA_OUTPUT_DIR>/reports/run_<run_id>.csv` and `.json`)

One row per input row, columns:
`line_no, doc_number, amount, kind, base_booking, carrier, eta, eta_source, eta_is_actual, eta_rescue, cutoff,
in_window, notif_count, notif_defaulted, invoice_id, balance, total, bill_email, route, new_doc_number, subject,
vship_booking_id, actions_planned, actions_done, status, message, warnings`
(`eta_rescue` = `EtaResult.details.get("rescue", False)` — rows whose ETA came from a carrier's rescue-only
fallback, 06 §7.5, are also listed as warnings in the summary).
The console summary groups identical failure messages per carrier, e.g. `MSC: 287 bookings failed — The MSC
access token expired or was rejected (HTTP 401)…`, instead of printing the same line hundreds of times.
The JSON file contains the same plus `run_id`, settings summary (no secrets), phase timings, and versions.

## 8. Console summary format (example)

```
Plan (run 20261105_093000, 494 rows, cutoff Mon 2026-11-16 09:30)
  NOTIFY ......... 212   (e-mails to send)
  PAID_UPDATE .... 31
  FUTURE_UPDATE .. 74
  BEN ............ 15
  BINDU .......... 28
  ACCOUNTING ..... 3
  SKIPPED ........ 30
  CUSTOMS_HOLD ... 2
  FAILED ......... 99
Warnings: 4 (see report)
```

## 9. `ledger.py`

```python
class Ledger:
    def __init__(self, path: Path): ...      # <ETA_STATE_DIR>/ledger.jsonl ; loads an index of e-mail events at init
    def record(self, *, run_id: str, doc_number: str, invoice_id: str | None, base_booking: str | None,
               action: str, detail: Mapping[str, Any], ok: bool) -> None   # append one JSON line, flush+fsync
    def emailed_on(self, invoice_id: str, day: date) -> datetime | None    # time of a successful QboSend that day
```
Never written in dry-run. Corrupt lines are skipped with a WARNING.

## 10. Tests (see 12-testing.md for the full matrix)

The pipeline is tested end-to-end with fake clients (in-memory implementations of QboClient, VShipClient and
CarrierClient behind the same method names) and a `FixedClock`: one test per route and per failure template
in 01 §14, plus dry-run (no writes, no output files, report written), confirmation abort, `--only`, duplicate
rows, ledger same-day guard, D11 revert, circuit breaker, and interruption.

# 11 — Command-line interface, packaging and UX (`cli.py`, `ui.py`, `pyproject.toml`)

## 1. Entry points

- Console script `eta` (pyproject `[project.scripts] eta = "eta_automations.cli:main"`).
- `python -m eta_automations …` (same `main`).
- `scripts/run_eta.bat` (Windows double-click helper, §7).

`main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int` parses arguments with `argparse` (no extra CLI library),
reconfigures stdout/stderr to UTF-8 (`errors="replace"`), loads settings (`--env-file` or `./.env`),
configures logging, then dispatches to `asyncio.run(<command coroutine>)`. It returns the exit code;
`if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(main())`.

## 2. Commands

### `eta run [INPUT_CSV] [options]`
Runs the full pipeline (10-pipeline.md).

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `INPUT_CSV` | Path to the input `.csv`. If omitted, open the Tk file picker (§6). |
| `--dry-run` | Plan only: all reads happen, nothing is written anywhere (no QBO/VShip writes, no e-mails, no output files, no ledger). Plan report is still saved. |
| `--yes` / `-y` | Skip the confirmation prompt. |
| `--force` | Ignore the same-day e-mail ledger guard. |
| `--no-email` | Never send e-mail: NOTIFY rows only get their QBO ETA update and VShip ETA patch; the e-mails to send by hand are listed in `ToEmail_<run_id>.csv` (10-pipeline.md Phase 3 step 1). |
| `--only DOC [DOC ...]` | Process only rows whose doc_number or base booking matches (exact, case-insensitive). |
| `--limit N` | Process only the first N rows (after `--only`). |
| `--env-file PATH` | Use this `.env` instead of `./.env`. |
| `--log-level LEVEL` | Console log level (default `INFO`; file log is always DEBUG). |
| `--max-parallel N` | Override `ETA_MAX_PARALLEL_BOOKINGS` for this run. |

### `eta eta BOOKING [BOOKING ...] [--json]`
ETA lookup only (no VShip/QBO). For each booking: carrier, ETA, source, is_actual, in-window flag
(computed with the current cutoff), or the error. Exit 0 even if some lookups fail. Useful for parity checks
against the old tool and carrier websites.

### `eta probe {qbo,vship,msc,maersk,cma,aggregator,all} [--booking B] [--invoice DOC] [qbo flags] [--yes]`
Diagnostics per integration as defined in each integration spec's "Probe" section
(04 §10, 04b §10, 05 §10, 06–09 §10). Prints a human summary, saves redacted raw payloads to
`<ETA_STATE_DIR>/probe/<service>_<id>_<timestamp>.json`, and exits non-zero if the integration is not working.
`all` runs every configured **read-only** probe that has the arguments it needs.

Without flags every probe is read-only. QuickBooks write probes (each asks for confirmation; on production
they also require `--yes`; they take the run lock, 03 §14):

| Flag (with `probe qbo`) | What it does | Spec |
|---|---|---|
| `--write-test --invoice DOC` | Sets the ETA field to original+1 day, verifies, restores, verifies again | 04 §10 step 4 |
| `--prefs-roundtrip` | Proves Preferences can be written back unchanged and with only the subject changed | 04b §10 step 2 |
| `--send-test --invoice DOC` | Sends one probe e-mail to the internal test customer and records the human-confirmed verification | 04b §10 step 3 |
| `--restore-template` | Runs only the e-mail template crash recovery | 04b §10 step 5 |

Probes that call billable carrier APIs (CMA) print the number of calls they will make before running.

### `eta qbo-auth [--listen] [--port N] [--no-browser]`
Interactive OAuth helper (04 §5.4): paste-back flow by default (works with production keys; the
redirect URI is `QB_REDIRECT_URI`); `--listen` uses a one-shot `http://localhost:<port>/callback` listener
(development/sandbox keys only). Stores the refresh token in the TokenStore and `.env`.

MSC options (06 §10): `eta probe msc --sandbox [--save-raw]` (public mock sandbox, no credentials),
`--token-info` (no network), `--booking EBKG… [--booking …]` (repeatable), `--compare` (bridge vs. official
API side by side; exit 1 on any difference).

### `eta msc-token`
Prompts (hidden input, `getpass`) for an MSC access token copied from the user's own signed-in myMSC browser
session (06 §2.2), stores it in the TokenStore and prints its status (seconds left, `iss`/`aud`/`exp`).
Needed only while MSC runs in `mymsc` bridge mode.

### `eta qbo-fields --invoice DOC`
Lists the custom fields on the given invoice (name, DefinitionId, type, value) so the user can confirm
`QB_ETA_DEFINITION_ID` / `QB_ETA_FIELD_NAME`.

### `eta version`
Prints the program version, Python version and the installed versions of httpx/pandas.

## 3. Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Completed (row-level failures are normal and go to the output files) |
| 1 | Unexpected crash (traceback printed and written to the log) |
| 2 | Configuration or authentication preflight error |
| 3 | Aborted at the confirmation prompt (or non-interactive without `--yes`) |
| 4 | Run completed, but the invoice e-mail path was unavailable or failed (NOTIFY rows reported as failed; see 04b) |

## 4. Console output

- INFO lines mirror the original's progress prints so staff recognise them, e.g.
  `Processing: EBKG17208602`, `  [Carrier] Identified as MSC — querying tracking API...`,
  `  ETA: 2026-11-16 | In 6-day window: True`, `  [OK]    #EBKG17208602`.
  In the concurrent plan phase, prefix each row's lines with `[line/total]` and emit them as a single block
  when the row's plan is complete (so lines from different rows do not interleave).
- Never print secrets (03-foundations §11).

## 5. Double-click mode (parity with the original's Tk + "Press ENTER" behaviour)

If `main()` receives **no arguments at all** (`argv == []`):
1. Behave like `eta run` with the Tk file picker.
2. At the very end (success, failure or crash) print `\nPress ENTER to close this window...` and wait for
   input (`EOFError` ignored) — parity with `pause_before_exit()`.
3. The confirmation prompt (10-pipeline.md Phase 3) still applies.

## 6. `ui.py` — Tk file picker (port of `tinkyWinky.get_user_inputs_authed`)

```python
def pick_input_file() -> Path | None:
    """Small Tk window titled 'ETA Tool' with: label 'FileName', entry (width 42), 'Browse...' button
    (filedialog.askopenfilename(title='Select .csv file', filetypes=[('CSV Files', '*.csv')])),
    'Cancel' and 'Submit' buttons; Enter submits, Esc cancels. Submit validates with
    is_valid_csv_file(path) -> (ok, reason): exists, is a file, suffix .csv (case-insensitive); on failure
    messagebox.showerror('Invalid file', reason) and stay open. Returns the Path, or None if cancelled."""
```
`tkinter` is imported lazily inside the function. If it is unavailable (e.g. headless Linux), raise
`ConfigError("No input file given and no GUI available — pass the CSV path: eta run <file.csv>")`.
Credentials are **never** collected through the GUI any more — they come from `.env`.

## 7. `scripts/run_eta.bat`

```bat
@echo off
cd /d "%~dp0\.."
if exist ".venv\Scripts\python.exe" (
  ".venv\Scripts\python.exe" -m eta_automations %*
) else (
  python -m eta_automations %*
)
```
(With no arguments this triggers double-click mode, §5.)

## 8. Program README (`README.md` at repo root, written by the implementer)

Must contain, in this order: what it does (one paragraph); requirements (Python 3.12+, no browser);
install (`python -m venv .venv`, activate, `pip install -e .[dev]` or `pip install .`); configuration
(copy `.env.example` → `.env`; the variable table from 02-configuration.md); first-time setup checklist
(13-rollout-checklist.md, condensed); daily usage (`eta run file.csv --dry-run`, then `eta run file.csv`);
output files table (01 §14); troubleshooting (auth errors → which probe/command; carrier not configured;
"already e-mailed today"); safety notes (sends real customer e-mails; use QBO sandbox / `--dry-run` first).

## 9. `pyproject.toml` essentials

```toml
[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=69"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "eta-automations"
version = "1.0.0"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = ["httpx>=0.28,<1", "python-dotenv>=1.0", "pandas>=2.2"]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = ["pytest>=8", "pytest-asyncio>=0.24", "respx>=0.22"]
# plus any extra an integration spec defines (e.g. an e-mail backend in 04)

[project.scripts]
eta = "eta_automations.cli:main"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
testpaths = ["tests"]
```

# 12 — Testing strategy and test matrix

## 1. Principles

- `pytest -q` must pass with **no network access**. Add an autouse fixture in `tests/conftest.py` that
  fails any test performing an un-mocked HTTP request (respx with `assert_all_mocked=True`, plus a guard
  that patches `httpx.AsyncClient.send` outside respx contexts to raise).
- Every pure rule in 01-business-rules.md has table-driven tests whose expected values are the golden values
  in that file (they were produced by running the original code).
- Every integration client (04–09) is tested with respx against the fixtures given in its spec file. Fixture
  files are created **verbatim** from the code blocks in the spec files (`tests/fixtures/<service>/<name>.json`).
- The pipeline is tested end-to-end with in-memory fakes (no respx needed) and a `FixedClock`.
- Time is always injected (`FixedClock`); tests never depend on today's date.
- Tests run on Windows and Linux (use `tmp_path`, never hard-coded paths; compare text files with `\n`).

## 2. Layout

```
tests/
  conftest.py                  # network guard, FixedClock fixture, settings factory, tmp dirs, fake services
  fakes.py                     # FakeQbo, FakeVShip, FakeCarrier (same method names as the real clients)
  fixtures/qbo/…  fixtures/vship/…  fixtures/msc/…  fixtures/maersk/…  fixtures/cma/…  fixtures/dcsa/…  fixtures/aggregator/…
  test_rules.py                # classification, routing, suffix, malformed message, duplicates, header skip
  test_business_days.py        # 01 §5 golden vectors (all 22 rows) + in_window boundary cases
  test_texts.py                # 01 §8 all 8 subject goldens + unreachable branch; 01 §10 note texts
  test_vship_logic.py          # 05 §9 tests 1–3
  test_vship_client.py         # 05 §9 tests 4–9
  test_qbo_*.py                # tests listed in 04
  test_carrier_msc.py          # tests listed in 06
  test_carrier_maersk.py       # tests listed in 07
  test_carrier_cma.py          # tests listed in 08
  test_dcsa.py, test_aggregator.py, test_router.py   # tests listed in 09 + router tests below
  test_http.py                 # retry/backoff/idempotency/Retry-After/redaction
  test_token_store.py          # atomic write, corrupt file, is_fresh skew, JWT exp parsing
  test_config.py               # required vars, booleans, legacy names, carriers None when unconfigured
  test_outputs.py              # exact bytes of every output template, BOM only on new CSV, append mode
  test_ledger.py               # record/emailed_on, corrupt line skipped, not written in dry-run
  test_pipeline.py             # end-to-end matrix (§4)
  test_cli.py                  # argument parsing, exit codes, double-click mode (monkeypatched input/Tk)
```

## 3. Unit test highlights (in addition to those listed in each spec)

**Rules (`test_rules.py`)**
- Every example row of 01 §3 (doc_number, amount) → (kind, base, route).
- Router table 01 §4: `EBKG17208602`→MSC; `267546627`→Maersk; `2675466270`→ref-number error;
  `NAM1234567`→CMA; `S312345678`→Grimaldi error text exactly; `XYZ`→no-pattern error text exactly;
  `EBKG17208602 C 2`→D6 error; lower-case `ebkg17208602`→MSC (D5).
- `with_arrival_suffix`: `EBKG12345678`→`EBKG12345678 A`; `EBKG12345678 A`→`EBKG12345678 AA`.
- Malformed message equals the 01 §7.1 template for amount `abc` and for a 1-column row.

**HTTP (`test_http.py`)**
- GET 503 twice then 200 → returns 200, 3 calls; Retry-After `2` honoured (patch `asyncio.sleep` and assert the delay).
- POST 500 → no retry (1 call) → `ServiceError`; POST 503 → retried; POST ReadTimeout → not retried.
- ConnectError on POST → retried.
- `ServiceError` message contains redacted body excerpt ≤ 500 chars and the `intuit_tid` request id when present.
- `redact()` masks `Authorization`, `password`, `refresh_token`, `Consumer-Key`, `KeyId`, `Bearer …` in strings and query params.

**Token store**
- `put` then `get` across instances; file mode 0600 on POSIX; corrupt JSON → warning + empty;
  `is_fresh` false within the 120 s skew; JWT `exp` extraction from the 05 §9 sample token.

## 4. Pipeline matrix (`test_pipeline.py`)

Use `FixedClock(datetime(2026, 11, 5, 9, 30))` (cutoff Mon 2026-11-16 09:30) and fakes. Each case asserts the
route, the actions executed (in order) against the fakes, the exact output-file contents, and the counters.

|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | `EBKG10000001,2450.00` | ETA 2026-11-03 (arrived), notif (0,True), invoice unpaid, BillEmail set | NOTIFY; QBO update(eta=11-03, doc→`EBKG10000001 A`); send subject `…****ARRIVED ON 11/03. PLEASE PLEASE PAY AND CLEAR THE CARGO****` (old DocNumber in subject); note `ARRIVED ON 11/03. NOTIF #1`; patch `2026-11-03T00:00:00`; ok=1 |
| P2 | `EBKG10000002 A,2450.00` | ETA 2026-11-03, notif (1,True) | NOTIFY; doc→`EBKG10000002 AA`; subject `…PLEASE PAY AND CLEAR THIS PAST DUE INVOICE AND CLEAR THE CARGO****`; note `…NOTIF #2` |
| P3 | `NAM1000003,1800` | ETA 2026-11-12 14:00 (CMA-style time; future, in window), notif (0,True), unpaid | NOTIFY; **no** doc change; subject `…***ESTIMATED ARRIVING ON 11/12. PLEASE MAKE PAYMENT ARRANGEMENT****`; note `ARRIVING ON 11/12.`; patch `2026-11-12T14:00:00` |
| P4 | `EBKG10000004,5000` | ETA 2026-11-03, invoice paid (balance 0) | PAID_UPDATE; QBO update(eta) only (no doc change, no send, no note); patch |

| P15 | `EBKG10000015 AA,5000` | — | BEN |
| P16 | `EBKG10000016 R,5000` | — | SKIPPED; no file entry |
| P17 | `NAM1000017 C,5000` | — | FAILED entry is exactly `NAM1000017 C` |
| P18 | `EBKG10000018,abc` | — | FAILED malformed template |
| P19 | carrier raises `CarrierLookupError("boom")` | — | `[ERROR] #… - Carrier Lookup Failed.\nboom\n` |
| P20 | carrier raises `NoEtaError("none")` | — | `[ERROR] #… -  Can't determine ETA.\nnone\n` |
| P21 | carrier raises `CustomsHoldError` | — | PotentialCustomsHold line exact; failed+1 |
| P22 | carrier raises `RuntimeError("x")` | — | `Unexpected error during carrier lookup.` entry |
| P23 | notif lookup raises; `ETA_ON_NOTIF_LOOKUP_ERROR=send` | VShip id lookup fails | NOTIFY planned with warning; apply: QBO update+send OK, note fails → `Note Write Error, QB Invoice Processing Successful`; failed=1 |
| P24 | same with `=fail` | — | FAILED `VShip notification lookup failed, nothing sent` |
| P25 | QBO send fails after doc change | — | FAILED `QB Invoice Processing Error, No Email Sent` + `(invoice number reverted to …)`; revert call made (D11); no VShip writes |
| P26 | VShip PATCH fails | — | FAILED `Booking ETA Change Failed, QB Invoice Processing Successful`; counted failed (D12) |
| P27 | invoice without BillEmail | — | FAILED `QB Invoice Processing Error, No Email Sent\nInvoice has no customer e-mail address (BillEmail)` |
| P28 | ledger shows e-mail today for that invoice | — | FAILED `[SKIP] … already e-mailed today at HH:MM (ledger); use --force to resend`; with `force=True` → NOTIFY |
| P29 | duplicate doc_number rows | — | second → `[SKIP] #… - duplicate row in input file (line N)` |
| P30 | dry-run over P1–P29 inputs | — | no fake write methods called, no output files, ledger untouched, report written |
| P31 | 6 consecutive MSC rows whose fake raises `CarrierLookupError("MSC login rejected")` (identical text) | — | 6th row fails fast with the circuit-breaker message; the fake carrier was called only 5 times. Control: 6 rows raising `CarrierLookupError(f"no record of booking {b}")` (texts differ) → fake called 6 times, breaker never trips |
| P32 | confirmation declined | — | exit code 3, no writes |
| P33 | `prepare_for_sending` raises `EmailPathUnavailableError("not verified")` | P1 + P4 + P7 inputs | P1 (NOTIFY) FAILED `QB Invoice Processing Error, No Email Sent\nnot verified`, **no** QBO update for it; P4/P7 applied; exit code 4 |
| P34 | `send_invoice` raises `TemplateRestoreError` on the 1st of 3 NOTIFY rows (parallel=1) | — | 1st row FAILED (+ D11 revert attempted); 2nd/3rd FAILED without any QBO call; non-NOTIFY rows still applied; exit code 4 |
| P35 | `--no-email` with P1 input | — | QBO update with `doc_number=None`, no send, no VShip comment, VShip patch done; `ToEmail_<run_id>.csv` row with subject, `EBKG10000001 A`, `ARRIVED ON 11/03. NOTIF #1`; status OK |
| P36 | DocNumber in `qbo.ambiguous` | — | FAILED `QB Invoice Processing Error, No Email Sent` + the AmbiguousInvoiceError text (D21) |
| P37 | two rows `NAM1000037` and `NAM1000037 A` | — | the fake CMA client's `get_eta` called **once** (router memo, 10 §6) |
| P38 | a second `run()` while the first holds `run_lock` | — | `RunLockedError` → exit code 2; dry-run is not blocked |

## 5. Optional live smoke tests

Marked `@pytest.mark.live` and skipped unless `ETA_LIVE_TESTS=1`: run each probe (read-only) against real
services using `.env`. Never part of the default run; never send e-mail.

## 6. Definition of done

- `pip install -e .[dev] && pytest -q` passes on Python 3.12 and 3.13.
- `eta --help`, `eta run --help`, `eta probe --help` work.
- `test_cli.py` runs `main(["run", "<tmp>/sample_input.csv", "--dry-run"])` end-to-end with
  `eta_automations.pipeline.build_services` monkeypatched to yield the fakes from `tests/fakes.py`
  (production code never imports from `tests/`).
- No Playwright/Selenium/browser dependency anywhere (`pip list` check in a test: importing the package must
  not import any of them).
